WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Yassamin Ansari (D-Ariz.) and Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet led U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), and Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) to introduce the Stop Orphaned Wells Act, legislation that would prevent oil and gas companies from abandoning oil wells on public lands, a practice that shifts well cleanup costs from oil and gas companies to the American taxpayer.

“Trump asked oil and gas executives to bankroll his campaign with a $1 billion contribution in exchange for a big payback. Meanwhile, Americans are left footing the bill for the damage they leave behind,” said Ansari. “Orphaned wells threaten our water, wildlife, and air. I’m proud to lead the effort alongside Senator Bennet to make the oil and gas industry clean up its own mess. Our bill would ensure oil and gas companies pay to clean up the wells they abandon.”

“For too long, taxpayers have footed the bill to clean up abandoned wells after companies walk away from their responsibilities,” said Bennet. “As the Trump administration moves to weaken the safeguards that hold companies accountable, Congress must protect taxpayers and the public lands that power Colorado’s outdoor economy, while making sure oil and gas companies pay the cost of cleanup, rather than Colorado's future generations.”

“Across California, there are over 5,000 orphaned oil wells that pose a threat to the health and safety of our communities and the environment,” said Padilla. “When wells are left abandoned, drinking water is polluted, greenhouse gases are emitted, and the climate crisis is accelerated. This bill will help ensure orphaned oil and gas wells are plugged so Californians and communities across the country are protected from toxic emissions and contaminated air and water.”

“Abandoned wells put Colorado communities in danger,” said Hickenlooper. “As Governor, we capped as many of these wells as we could, and that work continues here in the Senate, where we’re protecting taxpayers from getting stuck with the bill. Capping wells creates jobs and lowers pollution. It’s a win-win.”

“Oil companies can’t just walk away from abandoned oil and gas wells and leave taxpayers to bear the cleanup costs,” said Schiff. “I’m joining Senator Bennet and other colleagues to make sure that Big Oil is responsible for cleaning up their messes. Americans should not have to deal with the consequences of an oil company’s negligence.”

“In New Mexico and across the country, abandoned wells pose serious environmental harm and threaten the health of our communities,” said Luján. “We must ensure that oil and gas companies are held accountable and that taxpayers are not on the hook for the cost of cleanup. I've long fought to address abandoned wells, including championing the REGROW Act that was passed into law, and continue to work to ensure we identify and plug the thousands of abandoned wells nationwide. That’s why I’m cosponsoring this legislation to prevent companies from abandoning their wells and help reduce the number of abandoned wells in New Mexico and across the country.”

“When an oil and gas company goes bankrupt, New Mexicans shouldn’t be the ones left to pick up the tab for cleanup costs,” said Heinrich. “Right now, the Trump administration is making it easier for these companies to walk away without enough money set aside to clean up their wells. The Stop Orphaned Wells Act ensures that companies set aside money to meet their cleanup responsibilities, so taxpayers aren’t left paying the bill.”

Until 2024 when the Biden administration added agency rules, oil and gas fiscal assurance requirements were minimal, leading companies to abandon wells instead of remediating the land after drilling. The Trump administration is now rolling back these essential protections for public lands and American taxpayers. Nationwide, there are currently over 140,000 documented orphaned wells, including more than 15,000 on federal lands, and hundreds of thousands more that may be orphaned. Additionally, the number of documented orphaned wells in the United States has more than doubled since 2020. These sites are not only a significant liability for taxpayers and a growing threat to water resources, air quality, wildlife habitat, and private lands, but also jeopardize public health, ecosystems, grazing lands, outdoor recreation sites, and cultural resources that are at high risk from contamination.

This legislation is supported by 20 organizations, including Earthjustice Action, Colorado Fiscal Institute, Conservatives for Responsible Stewardship, Conservation Colorado, Montana Wildlife Federation, National Parks Conservation Association, Natural Resources Defense Council, Nevada Wildlife Federation, New Mexico Wildlife Federation, Public Land Solutions, Rocky Mountain Wild, San Juan Citizen’s Alliance, Sierra Club, Taxpayers for Common Sense, Trout Unlimited, Western Colorado Alliance, Western Organization of Resource Councils, Western Resilience Center, Wild Montana, Wilderness Workshop, and The Wilderness Society. In addition, this legislation was endorsed by U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee.

title: Ansari, Bennet, Padilla, Hickenlooper, Schiff, Luján Introduce Legislation to Protect Public Lands and Taxpayers from Orphaned Oil and Gas Wells

SAN ANTONIO, TX — Today, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) hosted a field hearing in San Antonio, entitled, “Examining the Community Impacts of Mass Deportation and Proposed ICE Warehouse.” He was joined by elected officials at the dais including Texas State Senator Roland Gutierrez (TX-19), Texas State Senator José Menéndez (TX-26), Texas State Representative Barbara Gervin-Hawkins (HD-120), Councilwoman Phyllis Viagran, City Council District 3. Hearing witnesses included Kristin Etter, Director of Policy and Legal Services, Texas Immigration Law Council, Priscilla Olivarez, Managing Policy Attorney with the Immigrant Legal Resource Center, and the Reverend Father Jimmy Drennan, St. Margaret Mary Catholic Church, COPS/Metro Alliance. Additional San Antonio leaders expressed their support for the hearing, including Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones and Councilman Ric Galvan, City Council District 6.

“San Antonio is one of the epicenters for ICE activity and ranks fourth in the nation for arrests,” said Congressman Castro. “The first American citizen shot by ICE, Ruben Ray Martinez, was a son of San Antonio. South of the city, the Dilley Trailer Prison has locked away thousands of children without proper food, medical care, and schooling. Texas National Guardsmen and local police in Texas have been deputized by ICE, supercharging arrests and detentions. Our community has become collateral damage in Trump’s mass deportation machine. Now this proposed warehouse on the East Side would extend these abuses deeper into our community and our lives. None of this is making life easier or more affordable for San Antonio families—it is tearing families apart, targeting our communities, and leaving a dark stain on our nation.”

“ICE is a rogue agency that shoots first and asks questions later. They are terrorizing our communities and torturing people with impunity,” said Senator Gutierrez. “The cruelty must end now”.

“The Trump Administration and Governor Abbott have colluded to stoke fear in our communities and incite human rights violations across our country. We must hold them accountable to protect people and restore basic human rights. Thank you, Congressman Castro and his team, for organizing a safe space for experts in the field and community members to discuss the threats to us all,” said Senator Menéndez.

“Today, I join U.S. Representative Joaquin Castro (TX-20) and other community leaders for a San Antonio field hearing to examine community impacts of mass deportation and the proposed ICE warehouse in San Antonio's East side in House District 120 that I represent. Like many faith leaders and others, I view the care and support of migrants not as a political issue, but as a fundamental obligation of human morality, compassion, and dignity. I will continue to fight for those that are being harmed and oppressed by this unjust system. I simply ask you to join us in this fight for human decency,” said Texas State Representative Barbara Gervin-Hawkins (HD-120).

“This was an excellent opportunity to work alongside my state and federal colleagues to identify a real path forward to prevent ICE facilities from entering the City of San Antonio. I am committed to working with my Council colleagues on a solid plan to address the inequities and impacts an ICE facility would have on our city, particularly on the East Side. I want to thank all of the community members who came out to listen, participate, and support their elected officials in this effort. Our panelists did an excellent job providing critical information and perspectives that will help inform our work as we move forward,” said Councilwoman Phyllis Viagran.

“A new detention center in Texas only works to expand the capacity to detain more of our community members and separate more families. The harm reaches beyond the household; we have seen that when parents and workers are detained, families lose income, businesses lose employees, and local economies lose the spending that helps them thrive. Our communities need investments that help families put down roots and thrive. We urge leaders to reject this expansion and focus on keeping Texas families, communities, and local economies together,” said Kristin Etter, Director of Policy and Legal Services, Texas Immigration Law Council.

“If the ICE warehouse is allowed to open, vital city resources will be misused to support the unlawful detention of our loved ones,” said Priscilla Olivarez, Managing Policy Attorney with the Immigrant Legal Resource Center. “I stand alongside the San Antonio community who are rightfully demanding DHS complete all federally mandated impact assessments before further steps are taken to open the ICE warehouse. San Antonio residents deserve to know the full adverse impact the ICE facility will have on those detained within its walls and the critical resources the facility will divert from our city.”

“What we are witnessing now is the re-institutionalization of discrimination in our law enforcement community, specifically ICE, against American citizens and our immigrant neighbors alike. People who are not properly vetted and not properly trained are coming into our institutions, and it is going to rip the fabric of our community apart unless it is brought to an end," said the Reverend Father Jimmy Drennan. “These are real people. I've looked into their eyes, and I've heard their stories. Their fear is real, and their fear is justified. In San Antonio, our community will keep pushing back.”

“I reiterate my opposition to the proposed ICE processing facility on San Antonio’s East Side. San Antonians deserve to feel safe taking their children to school, going to work, and calling police when they need help. Immigration enforcement must respect due process and basic human dignity,” said Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones. “We have pressed the federal government for transparency about this proposal, including its plans for the facility and the potential demands on our water, infrastructure, and emergency services. Our residents deserve answers, and our city deserves a meaningful voice in decisions that affect our neighborhoods. I thank Congressman Castro for convening this hearing and will continue demanding accountability on behalf of San Antonio,” said Mayor Ortiz Jones.

“We must continue to challenge every level of government to take action upon the acts of terror that ICE has committed upon our neighbors—noncitizen and citizen alike. We must demand the accountability of a rogue federal agency that continues to violate constitutional rights here in San Antonio and across our country. We must not back down from the fight. ICE has no home in San Antonio, and it must answer for its crimes against our community,” said Councilmember Ric Galvan.

"The first thing that Congress needs to do is pass a bill to shut down all of the infrastructure for these additional ICE buildings for the detention of human beings," said Bexar County Commissioner Tommy Calvert. "Congress should require the federal government to comply with local zoning regulations and health and safety measures as a check on unbridled tyrants."

“COPS/Metro represents 32 institutions across our city, and we have seen firsthand the impacts of detention and deportation. We are deeply concerned about the human toll of recent ICE arrests in our community and oppose the proposal for an East Side detention center. When parents are detained at workplaces, courthouses, or outside their homes, the harm reaches far beyond the individual. Children are left without caregivers, families lose their income, and entire neighborhoods live in fear. That fear has real consequences. Families are separated, children are kept home from school, and they hesitate to report crimes or cooperate with police. When people are afraid to take part in ordinary civic life, public safety and community trust suffer for everyone. We believe immigration enforcement must respect due process, family unity, and basic human dignity. We call on officials to: Limit enforcement actions at schools, hospitals, houses of worship, and courthouses; Ensure access to legal counsel for people in detention; Provide transparency about who is being detained and why; and pursue lasting, humane reforms to the immigration system. We stand with our immigrant neighbors and will continue to support families affected by these actions,” said Arturo Rodriguez, Leader, COPS/Metro Alliance.

Background:

San Antonio has become one of the cities hit hardest by Trump’s mass deportation campaign, ranking fourth in the nation in ICE arrests. Across Texas, the toll is reaching classrooms, with public schools losing more than 14,000 immigrant students last year. State leaders are continuing to deepen Texas’s role in ICE enforcement, requiring county sheriffs to enter 287(g) agreements with ICE. These agreements deputize local police officers as ICE agents, acting as a force multiplier for ICE arrests, detentions, and deportations. In August, Congressman Castro led a delegation of elected officials representing Bexar County urging cities to withdraw from their 287(g) agreements with ICE.

On March 25, 2025, San Antonio resident Ruben Ray Martinez was shot and killed by an ICE agent. Congressman Castro pushed for accountability when the news became public after the agency didn’t acknowledge its role in his death for nearly a year. ICE has also targeted children, detaining elementary students at their bus stops in San Antonio, including the Uzategui-Labrador family. These children and many others have been detained at the Dilley Trailer Prison, where children, some only a few months old, are held in inhumane conditions.

In January, ICE bought a nearly 640,000-square-foot warehouse on San Antonio’s East Side for $66.1 million. In August, it awarded a $17.3 million contract to GardaWorld Federal Services, the company behind “Alligator Alcatraz,” to retrofit the proposed detention facility and provide wrap-around services. The proposed site would hold 1,000 to 1,500 people daily.

Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05) yesterday introduced a package of bills designed to improve support for state and local election offices to improve voting access for Americans in future elections. The Accessible Voting Act will support state and local efforts to expand voter access, while the Dropbox Access Act will create a new standard by which localities must provide ballot dropboxes.

“Our democracy thrives when every eligible voter is able to participate, and these bills will remove barriers that all too often make it more difficult for Americans to cast their ballots. I’ve seen how expanding accessibility and access to ballot boxes has improved voter turnout and engagement in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania,” said Rep. Scanlon. “I’m proud to introduce these bills to advance more equitable and just voting policies for all Americans.”

The Accessible Voting Act, which Scanlon co-leads with Reps. Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Jamie Raskin (MD-08), and Lateefah Simon (CA-12), would support state and local election efforts through the establishment of the Office of Accessibility within the Election Assistance Commission (EAC). Specifically, the bill would ensure through the Office of Accessibility that state and local election officials are taking steps to obtain, deploy, and maintain voting systems, expand the number of options to cast a ballot in federal elections for older voters and voters with disabilities, and establish an online national resource center on accessible voting. The bill would also create a new state grant program through the Office of Accessibility for the improvement of accessible voting options, and reauthorize and expand grants through the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to improve voter accessibility for older Americans and people with disabilities.

The Dropbox Access Act, co-led by Reps. Simon and Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), would require each state to provide county-level secure drop boxes where individuals may drop off their completed ballots for federal elections. Specifically, the bill would prevent states from restricting voters’ access to drop boxes by requiring counties to provide, at minimum, one drop box per 20,000 voting-age residents, ensure that drop boxes are available 24 hours a day beginning 45 days before each election, and create more accessible options near public transit and for individuals with disabilities or with limited English-language proficiency, and for voters living in rural communities and tribal lands.

Scanlon introduced the voting accessibility bills package as the Trump administration has issued a series of executive orders and legislative proposals apparently designed to suppress voter turnout ahead of November’s midterm elections. Those proposals largely have been rejected by the courts. According to Scanlon, “now more than ever, it’s important that our elections reflect the will of the people, and that we challenge efforts by the current administration to undermine our election integrity.”

Recently, Congresswoman Scanlon convened hearings in her congressional district, at Widener University, and at the U.S. Capitol, to counter efforts by the Trump administration to spread disinformation about elections and disenfranchise voters with voter roll purges and by restricting access to mail-in voting. At both hearings, Members of Congress heard from election protection experts on voter protection and election security. Those experts expressed confidence in the safeguards and resiliency of our elections, and the importance of expanding access to the ballot box. Recordings of those hearings are available here: at Widener University, Chester PA and in Washington, D.C.

“American democracy works best when all citizens can participate and vote, no matter where they’re from, what language they speak or whether they live with a disability,” said Rep. Raskin. “Our Accessible Voting Act strengthens access to the ballot box and addresses a wide range of systemic deficiencies, so no eligible voter is left alone to overcome barriers to casting a ballot.”

“Our elders fought for our voting rights with blood, sweat, and tears – and yet too many people, particularly older Americans and Americans with disabilities, still face barriers to voting such as inaccessible polling locations or access to voter information. Both the Accessible Voting Act and Dropbox Access Act will improve voter accessibility for requesting mail-in ballots, accessing voter registration info, and when showing up to the ballot box,” said Rep. Simon. “As the first congenitally blind Member of Congress, improving accessibility to ensure that all Americans can equally access resources and participate in society is a top priority of mine. I am proud to lead on these bills with Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon to ensure ALL individuals can equally participate in local and federal elections to make their rightful voices heard.”

“The ability for everyone to have their voice heard is central to our American ideals—yet too often people with disabilities face unnecessary barriers in both registering to vote and casting their ballots, preventing them from fully participating in our democracy,” said Rep. Dean. “This legislation will help improve registration processes and eliminate barriers to voting, including by reauthorizing grants to improve voting accessibility for older Americans and those with disabilities. By breaking down these barriers, our communities can be better represented by every voice. I'm thankful to partner with Congresswoman Scanlon and Congressman Raskin to pass these essential bills.”

“We should be making it more accessible for Americans to vote, not harder,” said Rep. Garcia. “But the Trump administration and its Republican allies continue to attack voting rights and put up new barriers to the ballot box. That is why I am proud to once again co-lead the Dropbox Access Act, a practical bill to make sure voters have fair, accessible options to return their ballots. We should be protecting the right to vote, not suppressing it.”

PITTSBURGH, PA – October 2, 2026 — Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) alongside Rep. Chris Deluzio (PA-17) and Rep. Ro Khanna (CA-17), called on The University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC) to bargain in good faith with nearly 900 nurses, nurse practitioners, and midwives at UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital who have spent approximately eight months negotiating their first union contract.

In a letter to UPMC President and CEO Leslie Davis, the lawmakers raised concerns they have heard from workers and organizers about staffing levels, excessive workloads, and conditions that healthcare professionals say can make it harder to provide patients with the level of care they deserve.

The lawmakers specifically pointed to reports that nurses are routinely responsible for more patients than nationally recognized clinical standards recommend, including instances in which one labor and delivery nurse may be responsible for two or three patients even though professional staffing standards call for dedicated nursing care for a patient in active labor.

“For approximately eight months, nearly 900 health care professionals at UPMC Magee have been negotiating for a contract that reflects the critical role they play in caring for patients and families throughout western Pennsylvania,” the lawmakers wrote. “These workers have raised serious concerns about inadequate staffing, excessive workloads, and conditions that prevent them from consistently providing the level of care their patients deserve. UPMC has a responsibility to listen to these frontline professionals and work constructively to resolve their concerns without unnecessary delays.”

Contract negotiations between UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital, University of Pittsburgh Physicians, and SEIU Healthcare Pennsylvania began in January. UPMC reported that the parties held their 38th bargaining session on September 22 and have reached tentative agreements on several issues as negotiations continue.

These staffing concerns come as Allegheny County continues to face seriousracial disparities in maternal health. In 2023, the rate of preventable hospitalizations among Black women was 3.3 times higher than among White women in Allegheny County. The disparities are especially stark in Pittsburgh, where previous reports found that Black women were more likely to die during pregnancy than their peers in 97% of comparable U.S. cities.

Rep. Lee has made confronting the Black maternal health crisis a focus of her work in Congress, including pressing HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. during Black Maternal Health Week over threats to maternal health research and community-based programs, joining congressional efforts to expand access to midwifery care, and strongly supporting the Black Maternal Health Momnibus Act to invest in community-based care, strengthen and diversify the perinatal workforce, improve maternal health data collection, and expand maternal mental health support.

In their letter, Reps. Lee, Deluzio, and Khanna emphasized that safe staffing and workplace protections are critical to patient safety, retaining experienced healthcare workers, reducing exhaustion and burnout, and ensuring hospitals can respond effectively to emergencies.

“UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital is a vital institution that generations of western Pennsylvanians have relied upon for obstetric, neonatal, reproductive, and specialized health care,” the lawmakers wrote. “We will continue to monitor UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital actions closely and strongly encourage UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital, in accordance with the law, to bargain a fair contract in good faith with these workers.”

Workers at Magee have publicly advocated for staffing standards based on recommendations from national professional organizations. Those proposals include dedicated nursing care for patients who are laboring or being induced, as well as staffing standards for neonatal intensive care, postpartum care, emergency care, oncology, and other hospital units.

The full letter can be read HERE and letter text is below:

September 22, 2026

Dear Ms. Davis:

We write to urge the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC) to bargain in good faith, as required by federal law, with the nurses, nurse practitioners, and midwives at UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital. As you know, workers have a right to organize and advocate for improvements in their wages and working conditions, as well as engage in protected concerted activity under Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA).

We have received troubling reports from our constituents and organizers that nurses are routinely assigned more patients than nationally recognized clinical standards recommend. Nurses have described situations in which a single labor and delivery nurse may be responsible for two or three patients, even though established standards call for a patient in active labor to receive dedicated nursing care.

For approximately eight months, nearly 900 health care professionals at UPMC Magee have been negotiating for a contract that reflects the critical role they play in caring for patients and families throughout western Pennsylvania. These workers have raised serious concerns about inadequate staffing, excessive workloads, and conditions that prevent them from consistently providing the level of care their patients deserve. UPMC has a responsibility to listen to these frontline professionals and work constructively to resolve their concerns without unnecessary delays.

Safe staffing and other workplace protections are fundamental to patient safety, retaining experienced nurses, protecting workers from exhaustion and burnout, and ensuring that hospitals remain prepared to respond to emergencies.

UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital is a vital institution that generations of western Pennsylvanians have relied upon for obstetric, neonatal, reproductive, and specialized health care. We will continue to monitor UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital actions closely and strongly encourage UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital, in accordance with the law, to bargain a fair contract in good faith with these workers.

Thank you for your attention to these issues.

Sincerely,

Summer Lee

Member of Congress

Chris Deluzio

Member of Congress

Ro Khanna

WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) and Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11) introduced the bipartisan Submarine Cable Security Policy Act of 2026, which would streamline the Federal Communications Commission (“FCC”) permitting process for undersea cables while carefully vetting projects for national security concerns.

“Submarine cables are critical to our economy and national security, carrying the internet and communications traffic that Americans rely on every day,” said Congressman Menendez. “I am proud to co-lead this bipartisan legislation with Rep. Pfluger to establish a clear and consistent permitting process, provide greater certainty for responsible projects, and ensure that cables with potential national security risks receive the scrutiny they deserve.”

“Our foreign adversaries are investing in the undersea cables that carry over 95% of our international data, and they're doing it to undermine our national and economic security. The United States Submarine Cable Security Policy Act of 2026 sets clear, consistent security standards so we can keep bad actors out of our critical infrastructure,” said Congressman Pfluger.

The legislation would standardize the U.S. licensing process for undersea cables, establish national security requirements, set FCC review timelines, allow certain applicants to use self-certification and expedited review, and provide additional scrutiny for projects that raise foreign adversary or other national security concerns.

Read the full bill text here.

Congressmen Goldman and Bentz Introduce the IMD CARE Act for Patients Suffering from Serious Mental Illnesses
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Dan Goldman (D-NY) and Congressman Cliff Bentz (R-OR) introduced the IMD CARE Act, legislation which would expand Medicaid eligibility to include psychiatric care facility beds in excess of the current 16 bed limit for patients suffering from severe mental illness.
When the Social Security Act was enacted in 1965, it limited Medicaid funding to psychiatric facilities that had no more than 16 beds, resulting in a shortage of beds when the need for inpatient mental health care has grown.
The IMD CARE Act would amend the Social Security Act to establish a State Plan Amendment, allowing Institutions of Mental Diseases (IMDs) with more than 16 beds to receive Medicaid funding for all mental health patients.
Under current law, States that wish to receive federal Medicaid funding for IMDs with over 16 beds must submit a request for a waiver allowing them to receive Medicaid reimbursement for individuals needing psychiatric care.
These waivers are temporary, unstable, and require complex renewal negotiations.
The State Plan Amendment option included in the IMD CARE Act would provide predictable reimbursement structures, durable financing mechanisms, and greater continuity for patients and providers. States would be required to ensure a robust continuum of care including providing outpatient and community-based mental health care and wrap-around services. States would also be required to follow evidence-based clinical criteria for admitting and transitioning patients from institutional care.
The bill is endorsed by the National Association of State Mental Health Program Directors, National Association for Behavioral Health, Treatment Advocacy Center, National Shattering Silence Coalition, and Meadows Mental Health Policy Institute.
“Outdated Medicaid restrictions on long-term mental health care have left too many Americans in crisis without access to treatment,” Congressman Goldman said. “By allowing states more authority to expand their mental health services, we can reach more Americans who are stuck in a never-ending cycle of hospitals, jail, and the streets. This legislation is a critical step towards ensuring that everyone, regardless of income, can get the help they need with dignity.”
Said Congressman Bentz: “Studies show that a significant portion of the homeless and prison population suffer from severe mental illness. These people would benefit from the availability of proper treatment in our existing mental healthcare facilities. This bill would result in an increased number of beds and treatment available for mentally ill people. Without this improvement in how we deliver mental health services, those who need such treatment will continue to cost communities more in law enforcement and healthcare expenses. The circular progression of the mentally ill from the street to the hospital to the prison and back to the street must stop.”
“When someone on Medicaid is experiencing a mental health crisis, the program often won’t cover a psychiatric hospital bed. That’s because of a rule written in 1965,” said Scott Dziengelski, President and CEO of the National Association for Behavioral Healthcare. “A 60-year-old rule shouldn’t keep people from getting the care they need today. The IMD CARE Act takes an important step toward fixing that.”
Congressman Dan Goldman is committed to alleviating the mental health crisis in America. In 2025, he introduced the ‘Michelle Alyssa Go Act’ to increase the number of federal Medicaid-eligible in-patient psychiatric beds for individuals who are seeking treatment for both mental health and substance use disorders.
Full bill text here.

Yesterday, U.S. Representatives Rick Larsen (WA-02) and Mark Veasey (TX-33) reintroduced the America Votes Act to protect U.S. citizens who face disenfranchisement because of restrictive voter identification (ID) laws.

“As Trump and Republicans in Congress continue their unlawful attempts to suppress the right to vote, it is more urgent than ever to break down barriers to the ballot box,” said Rep. Larsen, a co-founder of the Congressional Voting Rights Caucus. “This bill builds on Washington state’s successful efforts to safeguard election integrity while getting rid of laws that disenfranchise citizens and prevent people from fully participating in democracy.”

“Voter ID laws are being sold as a solution to a problem that doesn't exist, and the people paying the price are eligible voters, especially in communities of color,” said Rep. Veasey, a founder and co-chair of the Congressional Voting Rights Caucus. “The America Votes Act protects every registered voter's right to cast a regular ballot by affirming their identity under oath. It's common sense, and it's time for Congress to act to protect the vote for all Americans.”

Despite claims that restrictive voter ID laws are necessary to prevent voter impersonation, there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud in the United States. Some state legislatures across the country continue to use excessively restrictive voter ID laws to target and deny certain Americans the right to vote. Restrictive voter ID laws disproportionately impact Black and transgender Americans, perpetuating the systematic disenfranchisement of certain groups in the United States.

In 2026, a total of 36 states require voters to show identification to cast a ballot, and 24 of those states require voters to present identification with a photograph. These identification requirements are in addition to those under federal law to register to vote.

The America Votes Act would establish new federal protections for registered voters to affirm their identity by submitting a sworn, written statement, even if they do not have a government-issued ID. Voters who sign a sworn, written statement can vote using a standard, non-provisional ­­ballot. The legislation is modeled on a successful Washington state law that allows voters to affirm their identity by submitting a similar written statement along with their mail-in ballot.

The full text of the America Votes Act is available here.

The America Votes Act is cosponsored by Representatives Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Betty McCollum (MN-04), André Carson (IL-07), and Julia Brownley (CA-26).

Larsen Fights to Protect Voting Rights

Rep. Larsen is a strong advocate for free and fair elections, expanding access to the ballot and Washington state’s vote-by-mail system. He has visited or plans to visit election offices in every county of Washington’s Second Congressional District to discuss the importance of safeguarding the right to vote with local officials ahead of this November’s elections.

Larsen first introduced the America Votes Act in 2012. The bill was included in the For The People Act, sweeping legislation to expand access to the ballot box, get dark money out of politics, end partisan gerrymandering and hold elected officials accountable to their voters. The For The People Act passed the House in 2021 but did not receive a vote in the Senate after Republicans blocked its passage.

###
title: Larsen Reintroduces Bill to Fight Discriminatory Voter ID Laws

At Kennedy’s Demand, DHS Finally Discloses Details of Batavia ICE Facility Expansion - New $17 Million Structure Will House Women Detainees

In a Response to Kennedy’s Letter Written in His Oversight Capacity, DHS's Own Numbers Show More Than 70% of Batavia Detainees Have No Criminal Record, Contradicting Administration's "Worst of the Worst" Claims

BUFFALO, N.Y. – Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26), a member of the House Committee on Homeland Security, today condemned the Trump administration's plan to build a new detention facility at the Buffalo Service Processing Center in Batavia at a cost to taxpayers of nearly $17 million funded by Trump and Congressional Republicans' Big Ugly Bill. He also exposed the administration's own admission that the vast majority of the people it is detaining in Western New York have no criminal record.

In a response to Kennedy's July 8 oversight letter, which arrived on September 29, 76 days past his July 15 deadline, the Department of Homeland Security disclosed that 72 percent of detainees at Batavia have no criminal record. Rather than defend the expansion as a public safety measure, DHS wrote that known criminal history "is not a prerequisite for immigration enforcement action." Secretary Markwayne Mullin instead pointed to the 2024 election, writing that the department intends to deliver "mass deportations."

"This administration told the American people it was going after the worst of the worst. Now they've admitted in writing that it isn't true. More than 70 percent of the people held in Batavia have no criminal record, and DHS says that doesn't matter," said Congressman Kennedy. "It took them more than two months to answer, and they still can't keep their story straight about what they're building. Meanwhile, the calls coming into my office tell the real story. Every single day we’re getting calls about people who are picked up by ICE while dropping their kids off at school or going to work. People that are here lawfully are feeling threatened and afraid. This administration must be held accountable.”

"Western New Yorkers are working hard to put food on the table, keep up with their utility bills, fill their gas tanks, and afford their medical bills. Our government should be focused on making life more affordable," Kennedy continued. "Instead, the Trump administration is spending nearly $17 million to enact its cruel and inhumane agenda.”

DHS's response contradicts itself. ICE's contract approval describes a "soft sided temporary detention facility," while DHS's answers refer to a "hard-sided" structure.”

The department also revealed that ICE plans to hold women at the new facility and that men could be held there as well "if the needs of the service dictate."

Kennedy's letter requested all records related to the decision to build the facility, including cost estimates and communications with contractors. DHS provided a single approval memo, with pricing details and the planned number of beds redacted. It said staffing levels for the facility are "still being discussed."

In July, Kennedy warned that the Trump administration has a pattern of rapidly building soft-sided tents and makeshift detention facilities without ensuring detainee health and safety, and demanded that DHS halt construction at Batavia. He will continue to press DHS for answers and to oppose the expansion of ICE detention in Western New York.

Read Congressman Kennedy’s oversight letter here.

Read Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s full response here.

###
title: Kennedy Condemns Trump Administration’s $17 Million Expansion of ICE Detention Facility in Batavia

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08) and Congressman Jefferson Shreve (IN-06) introduced the bipartisan Stop SIM Box Scams Act, which would ban the hardware that enables scammers to disguise robocalls as local telephone numbers.

In 2025, Americans received approximately 29.6 billion scam robocalls and texts and lost nearly $2 billion to these scams. By masking international or out-of-state calls with local area codes, scammers exploit trust and dramatically increase answer rates among unsuspecting victims.

“Scammers shouldn’t be able to use our area codes to rip off our communities,” said Congressman Menendez. “Our legislation bans the deceptive devices that allow scammers to masquerade as our neighbors, cutting off a key tool for fraudsters and protecting working families.”

“That ‘local’ Indiana number on your phone may be a scammer calling from halfway around the world,” said Congressman Shreve. “I wrote this bill to stop scammers from using these machines to pose as our neighbors.”

The legislation targets “SIM boxes,” which are specialized devices that house hundreds of SIM cards at once, cycling through local phone numbers to help scam syndicates flood individuals with robocalls and text messages while evading law enforcement detection.

The Stop SIM Box Scams Act would prohibit manufacturing, importing, selling, leasing, advertising, owning, or operating SIM boxes. It would also direct the Federal Communications Commission to coordinate with federal law enforcement to block imports and prosecute people who use them.

Read the full bill text here.
title: Menendez, Shreve Introduce Legislation to Ban Scam Call Machines

WASHINGTON – U.S. Representatives Jan Schakowsky (IL-09) and Mark Pocan (WI-02) on Thursday led a letter, signed by 71 Members of Congress, to Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy, Secretary of Homeland Security (DHS) Markwayne Mullin, and the commissioners of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), urging that the agencies ensure that Americans can continue to obtain genuine, non-controlled prescription medicines from outside the country.

New CBP procedures for international mail shipments, taking effect October 22, could disrupt 2.3 million Americans’ longstanding ability to obtain lower-cost prescription medicines from Canada and other countries for their personal use.

“For years, our constituents who have struggled with high prescription drug prices have obtained their medicines from pharmacies outside the United States, especially from Canada,” the members wrote.

“We support CBP’s goal of using better data to identify and intercept high-risk shipments. However, we are concerned that the new process could be implemented in a manner that prevents personal-use prescription medicines from being shipped to the United States or results in their routine refusal, including medicines Americans have long obtained from licensed pharmacies abroad,” the members continued. “Greater visibility should instead improve the government’s ability to distinguish dangerous products from lower-risk prescription medicines and preserve appropriate enforcement discretion.”

“We urge HHS, FDA, DHS, and CBP to delay any implementation of new procedures with respect to prescription medicines unless you can provide clear assurances that your agencies will not prevent genuine prescription medicines clearly intended for personal use and not appearing to present an unreasonable risk from entering the United States,” the members added.

“Americans should not lose access to affordable medicines simply because the government has better information about packages entering the country. We urge your agencies to use that information to focus enforcement on where the risks are greatest while preserving appropriate access to safe and affordable medicines for personal use,” the members concluded.

The letter is endorsed by the Campaign for Personal Prescription Importation, Just Care USA, National Association of Letter Carriers, Prescription Justice, and Social Security Works.

The full list of signers (71): Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Becca Balint (VT-01), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Brendan Boyle (PA-02), Nikki Budzinski (IL-13), Janelle Bynum (OR-05), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), André Carson (IN-07), Greg Casar (TX-35), Judy Chu (CA-28), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Steve Cohen (TN-09), Sharice Davids (KA-03), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Diana DeGette (CO-01), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Dwight Evans (PA-03), Lois Frankel (FL-22), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Jimmy Gomez (CA-34), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Timothy Kennedy (NY-26), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Greg Landsman (OH-01), Rick Larsen (WA-02), George Latimer (NY-16), Teresa Leger Fernandez (NM-03), Sam Liccardo (CA-16), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), John Mannion (NY-22), Doris Matsui (CA-07), Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08), Morgan McGarvey (KY-03), Jim McGovern (MA-02), Joe Morelle (NY-25), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-01), Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Chris Pappas (NH-01), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Brad Schneider (IL-10), Adam Smith (WA-09), Marilyn Strickland (WA-10), Thomas Suozzi (NY-03), Mark Takano (CA-39), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Paul Tonko (NY-20), James Walkinshaw (VA-11), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), and Frederica Wilson (FL-24).

Trump administration stopped processing new samples at the Region 6 EPA lab in August with no plan to protect Gulf Coast communities before the new Oklahoma lab is ready

Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07) called on Administrator of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Lee Zeldin to request a public meeting to explain how EPA will protect Houston and the Gulf Coast after halting essential work at its Region 6 Laboratory in Houston. The effort comes after the Trump administration ordered the Houston lab to stop processing new samples even though EPA acknowledges that its lab in Ada, Oklahoma will not be fully operational for months. EPA has presented no plan for testing air, water, and soil across five states if a hurricane or industrial accident strikes. The closure also upends the lives of the lab's scientists, many of whom may leave EPA rather than move 400 miles away. And many questions remain about the impact of moving the lab several hundred miles away will have on Houston’s public and environmental health following disasters.

“Housto is home to a large number of chemical plants and refineries, and this lab and its highly trained staff are essential to EPA’s mission of protecting human health and the environment,” Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher wrote. “In the case of extreme weather events, these scientists are among Houston’s essential first responders. Many EPA inspectors working on the Hurricane Harvey emergency response were based out of the Houston Lab. Moving the lab to a remote area exposes real infrastructure and logistics issues, which threatens Houston’s access to the critical air, water, and soil testing performed at the lab and the return of results as quickly as possible.

“Closing the Houston lab is ill-advised and I have advocated against it for years. At a minimum, EPA should present a comprehensive plan for how the lab’s functions will be carried out as this consolidation with Ada occurs,” Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher continued. “However, EPA ordered the lab to stop processing new samples on August 28, 2026, and EPA personnel communicated to my office during a meeting on September 9, 2026, that the Ada lab will not take over the Houston lab’s functions for several months… EPA has not articulated a plan for how new samples will be processed or how emergencies will be managed during this interim period. This is unacceptable and dangerous. With no plan in place, Houston and Region 6 residents cannot feel confident that the air they breathe and the water they drink will be safe if an industrial accident or natural disaster occurs.

“In light of these concerns, I request that EPA holds a public meeting in Houston by the end of 2026 to detail its plans for the continuity of the Region 6 Houston lab’s functions and receive input from impacted stakeholders and the public,” Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher concluded. “Additionally, I request answers to the following questions by October 30, 2026:

Has EPA developed a plan to ensure continuity of the Region 6 lab’s functions during the period from August 28, 2026, when the lab stopped processing new samples, to when the Ada lab is fully operational;

When will EPA communicate, in detail, its plans regarding management-directed reassignments to the Ada lab and relocating remaining staff to another Houston facility to the Houston lab’s current employees;

Once the Houston and Ada lab consolidation is complete, how will EPA ensure samples from the coast of the Gulf of Mexico are transported and processed in Ada in a timely manner;

What impact will the Houston and Ada lab consolidation have on the processing time of samples from the coast of the Gulf of Mexico? What, if any, analysis has been conducted on the potential public and environmental health impacts of delays caused by the consolidation? What was the result of this analysis; and

EPA personnel communicated to my office during a meeting on September 9, 2026, that the consolidation of the Houston and Ada labs will result in no detrimental impact on Region 6’s analytical capability. Please provide data substantiating this claim.”

The Region 6 Laboratory is a full-service analytical lab providing critical emergency response and disaster prevention services for five states. The Houston Lab is being moved from a newer facility built in 1990 to an older facility built in 1966, which is having to undergo extensive renovations to properly function. Since the EPA ordered Region 6’s lab functions to cease last month, the lab is in flux and operating in a diminished capacity, threatening Houston’s access to the critical air, water, and soil testing performed at the lab.

In 2019, Congresswoman Fletcher led an appropriations letter to the LHHS Subcommittee asking that they include language barring the EPA from using any funds to close the Region 6 EPA lab. Following this, Congresswoman Fletcher sent multiple letters to the EPA Administrator since 2019 in opposition to the lab relocation and a letter to the EPA Office of the Inspector General asking for an investigation into the closure. During EPA’s Fiscal Year 26 Budget Hearing, Congresswoman Fletcher raised this issue with Administrator Zeldin, who committed to looking into the issue.

To view the full text of the letter, click here.
title: As EPA Relocates Regional Lab Outside Houston, Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher Demands Public Meeting and Answers

Above: Gottheimer announces clawed-back funds for Andover Train Station.

ANDOVER, NJ – Today, Friday, October 2, 2026, at the future site of the Andover station, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) announced $500,000 in clawed-back federal dollars secured through the Transit Security Grant Program to strengthen security and safety at the planned park-and-ride station. The station is a key part of the effort to restore the Lackawanna Cut-off railway, with the goal of service from Scranton, Pennsylvania, to Hoboken, and on to New York City.

Every day, 28,000 people commute between Northeast Pennsylvania, Northern New Jersey, and New York. Sussex County has the longest average commute of any New Jersey county, at 38 minutes, and Vernon Township has been ranked as having the worst commutes in the state. Since 2011, New Jersey commute times have increased by 8.8 percent.

“There are zero options for folks in Sussex County to make their lives easier and get on a train to get to work or see a family member, and that has to change,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “I’ve clawed back $500,000 in new federal funding from Washington to Jersey, secured through the Transit Security Grant Program, to strengthen safety and security at Andover Train Station for the families and commuters who, ultimately, will count on it every day. This funding helps harden this site as the next phase of the project gets underway.”

Watch Gottheimer’s full remarks here.

The Andover site has already seen unauthorized access to the tunnel, including damage to or displacement of the measures meant to keep people out. The new resources can support security cameras, fencing, gates, and barriers, and other related security measures. This is capital security infrastructure that will stay with the station for the long haul and protect the public investment already in place.

The tunnel construction project is complete, with final details finished in June 2025, but there has been no construction activity at the site since. The project has $94 million in resources against an estimated total cost of $112.5 million. NJ TRANSIT plans to close the gap of about $19 million with state Transportation Trust Fund dollars and toll credits.

The project also promises real economic opportunity. According to Amtrak’s Corridor Vision plan, released in May 2021, expanding service beyond the Lackawanna Cut-off to Scranton could generate about $87 million in annual economic activity, plus $2.9 billion in one-time economic impact from construction along the corridor. More rail service also means fewer cars on the road, reducing emissions, highway congestion, and transportation costs and delays.

Today’s announcement builds on Gottheimer’s record of delivering for passenger rail in Northwestern New Jersey:

In 2018, Gottheimer sent a letter urging NJ TRANSIT to allow the community to upgrade the culvert, and NJ TRANSIT agreed soon after.

In 2021, he helped craft and pass the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which included $102 billion in total rail investment.

In 2022, he rallied state and local officials to push NJ TRANSIT to rebuild beyond the Cut-off. NJ TRANSIT committed $32.5 million to rehabilitate the Roseville Tunnel and the Hudson Farm and Junction Brook culverts, construct 8,000 feet of track bed, and stabilize rock slopes.

Gottheimer was joined by Andover Mayor Thomas Walsh, Andover Deputy Mayor Krista Gilchrist, NJTRANSIT Government & External Affairs Chief Paul Wyckoff, and Andover Police Chief Eric Danielson.

Below: Gottheimer announces clawed-back funds for Andover Train Station.

Read Gottheimer’s full remarks as prepared for delivery here:

It’s great to be back here in beautiful Andover, New Jersey, at the future site of the Andover Train Station, the park-and-ride station that is part of Lackawanna Railway, which, when it’s fully restored, will have service from Scranton, Pennsylvania, to Hoboken, New Jersey, and on to New York City.

I want to thank Mayor Thomas Walsh, Deputy Mayor Krista Gilchrist, and Paul Wyckoff of NJTRANSIT, and the rest of NJTRANSIT for joining us today. This is a project we’ve been working on together for many years now.

Thanks to great cooperation with our local elected officials here, when the railway is completed in 2031, Sussex County will finally have quality rail service on NJTRANSIT, helping commuters, stimulating tourism, and boosting the local economy.

Every day, 28,000 people commute between Northeast Pennsylvania, Northern New Jersey, and New York. Sussex County has the longest average commute time of all New Jersey counties, at nearly 38 minutes. Vernon Township has been ranked as having the worst commutes in the entire state. And since 2011, New Jersey commute times have increased by 8.8 percent.

Yet, there are zero options for folks in Sussex County to make their lives easier and get on a train to get to work, or to see a family member.

I’ve heard from so many residents, businesses, and local elected officials about this issue, and the urgent need for more transportation options to New York City from across Sussex.

Restoring the Lackawanna Railway is a key part of the solution, improving convenience and travel times for hundreds of thousands of travelers across the state, including right here in Andover and across Sussex County via NJTRANSIT regional rail.

Unfortunately, because of endless bureaucratic nonsense and constant stalling, this project has been trudging along for fifteen years.

Work on the Lackawanna project actually began back in 2011. But, it was paused in 2015 because NJTRANSIT could not access and upgrade the railway culvert on Hudson Farm. So, when I got to Congress, I joined with the Andover mayor and council – and went to work.

In 2018, working together, I sent a letter to NJTRANSIT urging them to allow the community, as they had asked, to upgrade a necessary railway culvert. Soon after, NJTRANSIT agreed to do it, a positive development after years of delay.

Then, in 2021, I helped write, negotiate, and pass the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which included $102 billion in total rail funding. In 2022, utilizing those dollars, I rallied state and local officials to push NJTRANSIT to rebuild beyond the Lackawanna Railway Cut-off, and NJTRANSIT committed $32.5 million to rehabilitate the Roseville Tunnel and the Hudson Farm and Junction Brook culverts, construct 8,000 feet of track bed, and stabilize rock slopes. The Tunnel, the track bed, and the culverts are already completed.

Not too different than when the B&O and then the Transcontinental Railroad were built, this project has been subject to repeated delays and uncertain timetables, with regulatory hurdles, red tape, property disputes, and inter-agency negotiations. But, many of us, including Mayor Thomas Walsh and Deputy Mayor Gilchrist, the council, and the Sussex County Community, have never given up – we’ve continued to fight – and, because of that, we’ve continued to achieve major milestones.

Today, I’m here to announce another important milestone in our work to bring the Lackawanna Railroad to Sussex County: I’ve clawed back $500,000 in new federal funding from Washington to Jersey, secured through the Transit Security Grant Program, to strengthen safety and security at Andover Train Station for the families and commuters who, ultimately, will count on it every day. This funding helps harden this site as the next phase of the project gets underway.

Let me walk you through where this project stands. NJTRANSIT is finishing the design and engineering scope for this next phase, with a target of the end of October.

The goal is to bring on a design contractor by the end of 2026, and begin design in January 2027. The design is targeted to be complete in January 2028, with construction bidding to follow, and construction on this station is targeted to be complete in August 2031, with service for passengers to follow.

Now, every one of those dates is a target. My job is to make sure NJTRANSIT hits each one of them, and I’ll be fighting to beat them, not miss them.

Right now, thanks in part to the dollars we clawed back to Jersey in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Bill I mentioned, the project has $94 million in funding against an estimated total cost of $112.5 million. That leaves a gap of about $19 million, which NJ TRANSIT plans to close with state Transportation Trust Fund dollars and toll credits.

The $500,000 I’m announcing today is separate. It will be utilized to prevent any delays in the timetable that could come from vandalism or damage from trespassers – including security cameras, fencing, gates, and barriers, and related protective technology.

The Andover Train Station has already seen unauthorized access to the Roosevelt Tunnel, including damage to the tunnel itself and to measures put in place to keep people out. This funding goes straight to help solve that problem. This is a critical station, and we cannot afford any setbacks, and we have to protect the investments the public has already made in the infrastructure here.

The benefits of this project are clear: Aside from all of the commuting benefits for families, so they can get to work and see their kids at night, an expanded transit network means fewer cars on the road, which will reduce vehicle emissions and pollution, highway congestion, and transportation costs and delays. This train will also result in real economic opportunity for the region.

That’s why, back in 2022, I also pressed the Federal Railroad Administration to restore Amtrak service on the Lackawanna between New York and Scranton – including a stop right here in Andover.

According to Amtrak’s own Corridor Vision Plan, expanding service from New York to Scranton, Pennsylvania, could generate about $87 million in annual economic activity, plus $2.9 billion in one-time economic impact from construction along the corridor.

I don’t know about you, but I can’t wait to see this railway running in 2031. I already have an alert set on my calendar.

When the Lackawanna Rail Line was first built back in 1911, it ran west for about 28 miles between Port Morris Junction in Port Morris, New Jersey, and Slateford Junction in Slateford, Pennsylvania. It was part of a 400-mile line between Hoboken, New Jersey, and Buffalo, New York. Imagine that. An incredible infrastructure feat for the time.

Passenger service on this corridor ended decades ago, between 1966 and 1971, and the tracks were later removed, leaving the line inactive for more than 50 years. So, part of this project has been putting in all-new tracks.

In the end, when it’s finished, I know this project will bring significant benefits to Sussex County and Northern New Jersey, to our families, to commuters, to deliver good-paying jobs for our hard-working men and women of labor, and to strengthen our communities by reducing congestion, improving commutes, boosting tourism, and helping grow our local economies. I look forward to continuing to work closely with Andover, Sussex County, NJTRANSIT, and Amtrak to bring quality, expansive rail service to North Jersey as soon as possible, without delay.

There is nothing partisan about this – it’s just about working together to solve problems for Jersey families.

If we continue to do that, to work together to restore Lackawanna and expand New Jersey’s transportation network, I know that, in the greatest country in the world, our best days will always be ahead of us.

May God bless you and God bless the United States of America.
title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Claws Back $500,000 in Federal Dollars for the Future Lackawanna Railway & Andover Train Station Site

NEWS: Ocasio-Cortez, Sanders, Merkley Unveil Ban Flock Act to Protect Americans’ Right to Privacy
Press Release
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14), and Senators Bernie Sanders (I-VT) and Jeff Merkley (D-OR) released the Ban Flock Act, legislation to put an end to the rise in AI-powered surveillance cameras that track Americans across the country. The Ban Flock Act would prohibit federal agencies from using automatic license plate readers (ALPRs) and block federal funding from state and local governments that use this technology.
“Across the country, Big Tech companies like Flock Safety have built a mass surveillance system to harvest Americans’ private and personal data without their consent. AI-powered cameras are keeping track of our every move and weaponizing this data against working people to make record profits. The widespread integration of this technology into American society is unconscionable,” Ocasio-Cortez said. “I am proud to introduce the Ban Flock Act with Senator Sanders to enforce our constitutional right to privacy and protect Americans from both corporate and government surveillance.”
“At a time of growing concern about the unchecked power of artificial intelligence, Flock is eviscerating the very notion of privacy by installing tens of thousands of cameras in communities across America without their consent,” Sanders said. “Going to the doctor? Flock knows. Dropping your kid off at school? Flock is tracking you. Flock is always watching. We cannot allow America to become a surveillance state where a handful of AI oligarchs profit by giving the government the power to track our every movement.”
“Your right to privacy includes the freedom to move around your community without every move being monitored,” Merkley said. “Right now, Flock is selling its cameras nationwide, laying the groundwork for a surveillance state while enriching corporate executives. No one should have this unchecked surveillance power at their fingertips, which is why I’m teaming up with Senator Sanders to rein in this dangerous technology.”
Flock is the largest vendor of automatic license plate readers in the United States, with more than 120,000 cameras across the country that scan and record 20 billion vehicles every month. Newer Flock cameras do not just record vehicles — they record people. Flock’s AI system can combine images of you and your vehicle with databases of phone numbers, relatives and court records to find out who you are, where you're going and why. The company also operates a national lookup tool, so agencies that contract with Flock can access data generated by cameras in another city or state. The national lookup tool searches can turn up massive amounts of information, including physical descriptions, records of an individual’s online accounts and lists of their relatives.
The mass surveillance capabilities enabled by Flock and other automatic license plate reader companies have threatened the civil liberties of everyday Americans:
- Flock has shared state information with federal immigration officials;
- Law enforcement officials have pulled Flock data to investigate activists and logged searches corresponding to protests against ICE raids, in support of Palestinian rights and for ‘No Kings’ demonstrations; and
- Officers have used plate readers to track wives, girlfriends, exes and women they wanted to meet without their consent.
So far this year, at least 56 municipalities have deactivated, cancelled, or rejected contracts with Flock. Congress must act to stop the mass surveillance of citizens.
The Ban Flock Act would do this by:
- Prohibiting the federal government from using automatic license plate readers or accessing the information they collect;
- Stopping federal grant funding from flowing to state or local governments that use automatic license plate readers or contract with automatic license plate readers companies;
- Allowing Americans to sue the federal government for violation of their rights through the use of automatic license plate readers.
Read the text of the bill here.

Montpelier, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, announced that the Williams County Health Department will receive a $125,000 Drug-Free Communities award through the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). The award will support the health department’s Educating Communities on Healthy Opportunities (ECHO) Coalition, which works to prevent substance abuse in youth and adults throughout Williams County.

“I am honored to partner with the Williams County Health Department to deliver vital Federal dollars to bring about meaningful change in people’s lives,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “Northwest Ohioans deserve resources and support to prevent and tackle substance abuse, and the ECHO Coalition brings that support right to our back doors. Their programs bring together people from all sectors of the county to provide the proactive approach to substance abuse and mental health that our communities so desperately need.”

“The Williams County Health Department's Drug-Free Communities (DFC) grant has strengthened substance use prevention efforts across Williams County by bringing schools, community organizations, healthcare providers, law enforcement, and youth together around a shared goal,” said Katie Lantzsch, the Williams County Health Department’s Director of Health Education and Preparedness. “The grant has expanded prevention education, empowered local youth to lead change in their communities, and helped build a stronger network of support to reduce risk factors and promote healthy choices for future generations.”

Through her role on the House Appropriations Committee, Congresswoman Kaptur has been instrumental in securing Federal investments for substance abuse prevention across our Northwest Ohio community. In July 2026, she announced two $125,000 DFC awards for EHOVE Career Center’s Future Leaders Program in Sandusky and for the Springfield Area Prevention Coalition in Swanton. Last week Congresswoman Kaptur announced that the Erie County Department of Health had been awarded an $800,000 grant award through HHS for Substance Abuse Treatment. Congresswoman Kaptur also delivered a $1.8 Million Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) award to the Erie County Health Department in 2023.

You can learn more about how ECHO serves our Williams County community by clicking here.

Hartford, CT – Today, Reps. John B. Larson (CT-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Jim Himes (CT-04), and Jahana Hayes (CT-05) responded to reporting from The Atlantic that President Trump is entertaining a plan to ease sanctions on Russia:

“When we voted against the Senate’s sanction bill this month, we warned that stripping out the enforcement language would leave every decision about punishing Putin to a president who keeps siding with the Kremlin. It took less than two weeks and President Trump is entertaining a plan to ease sanctions on Russia.

“Just last week President Trump went to the United Nations and bragged about the ‘enormous new tariff authorities’ this bill handed him. So, the one part of the law he seems eager to enforce will needlessly raise costs on Americans by continuing his reckless trade policies, while the power he was given to cripple Putin’s war machine he is already looking to sign away.

“That is exactly why the House-passed bill, H.R. 2913, required the president to act on sanctions. Without that requirement, sanctions are dependent on President Trump’s will to impose them – and President Trump has shown us time and time again he would rather be a friend to Putin than hold him accountable.

“We will keep fighting for military assistance for Ukraine and real sanctions that no president can waive away as a favor.”
title: Connecticut House Delegation Statement on Reports President Trump is Seeking to Ease Russian Sanctions

Rep. Vasquez Secures $96 Million to Build New Alamo Navajo Health Center
With HHS grant, Alamo Navajo Chapter will build a new, technologically advanced health center in their community
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) secured $96 million in federal funding from the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to build a new, technologically advanced health center at the Alamo Navajo Chapter. The health center will serve over 2,600 Tribal residents living in the communities of Alamo, Magdalena, and Socorro.
“This $96 million investment is a major step toward ensuring the Alamo Navajo community has access to the quality health care it deserves,” said Vasquez. “For too long, Tribal communities have been denied access to reliable healthcare – being forced to drive incredibly long distances and go to great lengths just to see a doctor. This project will bring care closer to home, and I’m proud to deliver this funding and will continue working to ensure the federal government is serving New Mexico’s Tribal communities.”
The $96 million award will support the construction of a new 70,000 gross square feet (GSF) health center and will be a modern, state-of-the-art, advanced facility to provide health care services specifically designed to meet the needs of the Alamo Navajo Chapter.
This funding comes from the Interior Appropriations bill, which passed with strong bipartisan support. Congressman Vasquez also secured key funding and resources for New Mexico in the bill, including $1,092,000 for the Ramah Navajo Drinking Water Improvement project and over $3 million in projects to improve public safety and infrastructure in Southern New Mexico.
Vasquez has consistently worked to support New Mexico’s Tribal communities:
- Led the Tribal HUD-VASH Act to provide housing assistance and support services for Native American veterans.
- Voted to extend the Special Diabetes Program for Indians to help address health disparities in Tribal communities.
- Championed the bipartisan Indian Programs Advance Appropriations Act to fulfill the US government's trust and treaty responsibilities and provide full and consistent funding for IHS and BIE programs.
- Led the Parity for Tribal Law Enforcement Act to enhance public safety within Tribal communities.
###
title: Rep. Vasquez Secures $96 Million to Build New Alamo Navajo Health Center

WASHINGTON, D.C. -- On September 24, Congressman Raul Ruiz, M.D. (CA-25) introduced H. Res. 1583 expressing support for the designation of October as National Promotoras Month. This is the first time the resolution has been introduced at the federal level.

Promotoras, sometimes known as community health workers, peer educators, health advocates, patient navigators, and cultural liaisons, are trusted messengers who connect families to the care they need. They serve rural towns, farmworker families, Tribal nations, border communities, and immigrant neighborhoods, delivering health education and prevention in the language and culture of the people they serve.

"As an Emergency Physician, I saw too many patients arrive when it was already too late. Promotoras change that. They knock on doors, speak our language, and earn the trust that keeps families healthy before a crisis hits. This resolution recognizes their work and thanks them for everything they do for our communities," said Congressman Raul Ruiz M.D.

Promotoras help reduce emergency room visits, increase preventive care, and improve management of chronic diseases like diabetes, asthma, and heart disease, lowering health care costs for everyone. Yet many remain underrecognized and underpaid, with limited training pathways and support.

The resolution:

Recognizes the essential contributions of promotoras and community health workers to the health of our communities

Acknowledges the need for sustainable funding, workforce development, and fair compensation for the promotora workforce

Encourages federal, state, Tribal, and community partners to invest in and expand promotora-led programs, especially in rural areas

"Promotoras are trusted community leaders whom families turn to for resources, information, and support. They show up during emergencies and celebrations alike, guided by the same deep commitment to provide “servicio de corazón”, service from the heart,” said Maria Lemus, Executive Director, Vision y Compromiso. “We are profoundly grateful to Congressman Ruiz for his leadership in presenting this federal resolution recognizing the vital contributions of Promotoras. Community members, as well as federal and state agencies, rely on Promotoras to advance the health, well-being, and resilience of communities across the country. Designating October as National Promotoras Month honors their leadership and ensures that their work receives the recognition it deserves."
title: CONGRESSMAN RAUL RUIZ, M.D. INTRODUCES RESOLUTION DESIGNATING OCTOBER AS NATIONAL PROMOTORAS MONTH
