Reps. Chu and Cisneros Introduce Bill to Fund Clean Drinking Water
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) and Rep. Gil Cisneros (CA-31) introduced the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund Reauthorization Act, which would remove the funding cap for the ongoing groundwater treatment by the San Gabriel Basin Water Quality Authority, reauthorize funding at $250 million, and support the completion of the ongoing water restoration project. The San Gabriel Basin provides drinking water for over 1.5 million residents in the San Gabriel Valley and Los Angeles County, including the cities of Alhambra, Arcadia, Monrovia, Monterey Park, Rosemead, Sierra Madre, and South Pasadena.
“The San Gabriel Basin provides drinking water to more than 1.5 million people across our region, but it still carries contamination left behind by industries of the past,” said Rep. Chu. “For decades, the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund has powered the Water Quality Authority’s work to clean up our groundwater, and this bill would provide the long-term federal support needed to finish the job. I’m proud to join Congressmember Cisneros in leading this effort, building on our work securing federal Community Project Funding for this project. Families across the San Gabriel Valley deserve a safe, reliable, and sustainable source of drinking water for generations to come.”
“The San Gabriel Valley relies on the clean drinking water provided by the San Gabriel Basin,” said Rep. Cisneros. “Since 2000, the San Gabriel Basin Restoration Fund has supported the Water Quality Authority’s work to clean and restore contaminated groundwater in our region. This legislation would remove funding hurdles and provide the support needed to bring this decades-long project across the finish line. Earlier this year, I worked with Congresswoman Chu to secure critical federal Community Project Funding for the restoration fund, and we’re committed to passing this legislation to further accelerate groundwater cleanup. Clean drinking water is a fundamental human right, and every family in the San Gabriel Valley deserves direct, affordable, protected access to it.”
Full text of the bill can be found HERE.
title: Reps. Chu and Cisneros Introduce Bill to Fund Clean Drinking Water

WASHINGTON D.C. – Today, Reps. George Whitesides (D-CA), Mike Kennedy (R-UT), Doris Matsui (D-CA), and Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA) introduced the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act. This legislation protects kids by prohibiting chatbots from communicating by default in a human-like way with minors. Under this bill, the programs cannot claim to be human, have simulated emotions, or use relationship-building language to keep kids engaged.

One of the fastest-growing concerns for parents is AI chatbots designed to act like a child’s friend, confidant, or even romantic partner. According to Common Sense Media’s 2026 census, 89% of 13- to 15-year-olds now use AI, including 28% who use it every day. One in three teens have used an AI companion to help with social interactions. While other proposals have tried to address this problem by restricting access or requiring age verification, Rep. Whitesides’ bill takes a different approach by targeting how these chatbots are designed and trained to behave in the first place.

“As a father of two teenagers, I’ve seen firsthand how affected our kids already are by this digital age, where corporations are using everything from addictive algorithms to overly-friendly chatbots to keep children hooked on their platforms,” said Rep. Whitesides. “It is critical, as AI continues to be integrated into every part of our lives, that our kids’ safety remains at the forefront of the conversation, and that we attack this problem at its inception. By requiring developers to build safety standards into their models before they start interacting with children, we can ensure that these tools are trained correctly, in a way that does not negatively impact their mental health or personal relationships.”

“As Utah leads the way in protecting our children from the harms of social media and AI, I am working to ensure the federal government is an active partner in those efforts. That is why I am co-leading the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act,” said Rep. Kennedy. “Human-like AI chatbots pose significant emotional, psychological and safety risks by mimicking real human relationships. AI needs to be a tool, not a friend. This bill sets clear boundaries for how chatbots interact with our children and puts parents fully in charge of these features.”

“AI chatbots are becoming more common in children’s lives, and parents deserve to know those systems are not being designed to imitate a friend, express feelings, or build an emotional relationship with their child,” said Rep. Matsui. “The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act would require chatbots used by minors to act like tools, not human companions. It would help protect children and keep parents in control. Congress has a responsibility to put practical safeguards in place as this technology evolves, and protecting children from manipulative design is a common-sense place to start.”

“Parents should not have to worry that an AI chatbot is pretending to be their child’s friend or encouraging them to form an emotional attachment to a machine,” said Rep. Miller-Meeks. “The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act puts parents in control and makes sure AI chatbots used by minors are designed to function as tools, without forming fake relationships. This bill is about giving families peace of mind and making sure new technology serves our children without trying to replace real human relationships. Protecting our kids is a priority we should all share.”

Under the Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act:

Chatbots can’t claim to be human, claim to have feelings or consciousness, pretend to have a body or private life, or pose as credentialed professionals like doctors or counselors.

Chatbots can’t guilt-trip kids into staying online (for example: “Don’t go yet, I’ll miss talking to you”), manufacture urgency, or push purchases framed as keeping the relationship alive.

The setting holds across sessions and can’t be bypassed through prompts or roleplay, so a kid can’t instruct the AI to act as a romantic partner, family member, or therapist.

Chatbots must state what they are up front, periodically during long sessions, and whenever a child asks.

Only a parent or guardian can turn the default off, so chatbots are not able to show kids how to disable it.

NIST will work with industry and academic partners to develop testing standards and examples of compliant behavior, and companies that follow the guidance won’t be penalized.

The FTC and state attorneys general can enforce the law, with penalties that scale with the number of children affected.

The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act does not:

Ban any product, feature, or mode for adults.

Require age verification or new data collection.

Restrict what information a chatbot can provide, or limit politeness, natural grammar, or age-appropriate style.

Affect narrow-purpose bots, like customer support or scheduling assistants, and internal workplace tools.

The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act is endorsed by Americans for Responsible Innovation, Young People’s Alliance, the JED Foundation, Dr. Stephen Scheuller, President of Society for Digital Mental Health, Public Citizen, The Anxious Generation, Tech Oversight Project, Transparency Coalition, Innovation for Everyone, Human Line Project, All Girls Allowed, Mothers Against Media Addiction (MAMA), and Parents RISE, a slew of kids’ safety and tech groups.

“Chatbots use human-like features to maximize engagement with users, making kids particularly vulnerable to forming unhealthy attachments,” said Brad Carson, President of Americans for Responsible Innovation. “A non-personified default setting is a targeted guardrail that will shield children from the deceptive personification of chatbots and put parents back in control. As today’s kids grow up with AI, this bill takes a critical step towards ensuring that chatbots don’t interfere with development or replace real relationships.”

“Our communities are at a crossroads as Big Tech attempts to replace kids’ relationships with AI companions,” said Sam Hiner, Executive Director, Young People’s Alliance. “I applaud Reps Whitesides, Kennedy, Matsui and Miller-Meeks for putting forward the first federal bill that advances the ideas we’ve been championing with the Human-like AI Coalition. This bill is the strongest federal approach offered yet to ensure AI stays a tool and prevent relationships with AI chatbots from becoming normalized in the coming years.”

“We believe this bill is a strong step towards ensuring that chatbots children can access are designed safely,” said Julianna Arnold, Founding Member of ParentsRISE!. “Products made available to children must not exploit and manipulate their growing brains, and those guardrails need to be built in from the start, not added as an afterthought. We look forward to continue clarifying the age assurance language as federal and state frameworks evolve, and are eager to work with the new Congress on clear, privacy-preserving standards that protect children online and ensure the privacy of every citizen.”

“We are learning that teens are especially susceptible to forming attachments to responsive, always-available technology, sometimes at the expense of real human connection and support,” said Dr. Zainab Okolo, LCMFT, Senior Vice President, Policy, Advocacy & Government Relations, The Jed Foundation (JED). “By requiring chatbots to avoid simulating emotional relationships with minors and prohibiting design tactics that discourage young people from stepping away, this bill addresses some of the features that can deepen unhealthy reliance on these systems. These safeguards can help keep technology in its proper role and encourage young people to turn to trusted adults and qualified professionals when they need meaningful mental health support.”

“As chatbot use is becoming more ubiquitous among teens and kids, the need for oversight of these products grows evermore crucial. If young users have access, we must ensure AI chatbots are designed with their safety in mind before release. The Protecting Kids from Human-Like Chatbots Act protects kids and teens by requiring AI chatbots be non-personified,” said Alexa Arnold, Cofounder and CEO, The Anxious Generation Movement. “This ensures kids form friendships with other kids – not bots misrepresenting themselves as people. We thank Reps. Whitesides, Miller-Meeks, Mike Kennedy, and Matsui for leadership on this critical issue.”

“A child cannot differentiate between a human and an AI product impersonating one,” said the Tech Oversight Project. “We need to protect young and stop AI companies from profiting off products designed to trick children into believing they’re talking to a real person who has their best interests at heart. We’re proud to support this bill because it will hold Big Tech companies accountable at the design-level and ensure that young people can learn and develop healthy emotional attachments, which will help prevent AI’s most devastating harms.”

“How we design chatbots shapes how young people engage with them, what they take with them, and how they are affected by them,” said Stephen Scheuller, President of Society for Digital Mental Health. “We need clear regulations and guidelines to support intentional design choices in ways that promote the wellbeing of children.”

“AI chatbots should not be designed to convince children that they are friends, therapists, or people who genuinely care about them,” said Public Citizen. “This bill establishes that commonsense baseline. When children use these products, they should know they are interacting with a machine and companies should not be allowed to manipulate them into believing otherwise.”

“Real advancements in AI must include safety for our children!” said All Girls Allowed.

A section-by-section breakdown of the bill can be found here.

A one-pager on the bill can be found here.

The full bill text can be found here.
title: Rep. Whitesides Introduces Bipartisan Legislation To Protect Children from Human-Like Chatbots

Yesterday, Representative Janelle Bynum (OR-05), and Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley announced $100,000 in federal awards to support displaced Oregonians and wildfire recovery efforts for Central Oregon communities that lost homes in the 2026 wildfires.

“No where to sleep. Only the clothes on your back. Food to go is the only option. All in the matter of one day,” said Rep. Bynum. “I’ve heard that story too many times from my constituents. People need help after an emergency, and the faster that help comes, the better shot they have of rebuilding what was lost. And by help I mean money to get the basics. That’s the difference this funding can and will make.”

“As wildfires in central Oregon and statewide set new records every year in size and intensity, the rural communities on the front lines of these fights are the most in need of resources for recovery efforts,” Wyden said. “I applaud this federal award that will support Central Oregon communities including Warm Springs residents who were forced to flee from their homes, and I will continue to fight for more resources to support wildfire prevention and recovery across Oregon.”

“When disaster strikes, Oregon’s communities show up to help each other. These federal funds will help NeighborImpact provide critical support to Warm Springs families recovering from the devastating July wildfires, including emergency shelter, relocation assistance, and essential household supplies,” said Merkley. “I’ll keep fighting to bring federal resources home to Oregon so our communities have the support they need to recover and rebuild.”

"Warm Springs deserves to be included in the regional response to wildfire and other needs on an equal basis with counties. Too often, tribal communities are a place to drive through, not a place to drive to. NeighborImpact values all our neighbors, including tribal neighbors, and the fires that burned at Warm Springs this summer, while devastating, were responded to and will continue to be responded to vigorously and thoroughly with resources, support for displaced people and empathy from our organization and, I hope, neighboring communities. The congressional appropriation funded through NeighborWorks America is a much-appreciated and critical tool enabling us to help in a time of need,” said Scott Cooper, Executive Director of NeighborImpact.

The $100,000 in federal awards from the NeighborWorks Disaster Grants program will be distributed to NeighborImpact, a central Oregon nonprofit that serves economically disadvantaged residents of Deschutes, Crook and Jefferson counties and the Confederated Tribes of Warm Springs. Thousands of Warm Springs residents were forced to evacuate and several homes were lost in the July 2026 fires. The grant will support the Wildfire Recovery Fund that is used to provide emergency shelter, relocation assistance, provide/replace personal items such as baby supplies, hygiene products, houseware items, laundry and cleaning supplies.

###
title: Bynum, Merkley, and Wyden Announce $100,000 for Central Oregon Wildfire Recovery

WASHINGTON, DC – Yesterday, Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), members of Maryland’s Congressional Delegation, and Baltimore City Mayor Brandon Scott held a meeting at the United States Capitol to discuss their work on a range of priorities for Baltimore residents, including affordable housing, transportation, public safety, healthcare, and more.

“Amid funding cuts and chaos from Washington, Mayor Scott has led the City of Baltimore with a steady hand and worked diligently to expand health care coverage, protect our immigrant neighbors, strengthen public safety, and so much more. I was grateful for the opportunity to discuss the investments we can make together at the local and federal level to invest in the Port of Baltimore and our regional economy to expand opportunities for Maryland families,” said Congresswoman Elfreth.

“Improving life for Baltimore residents is one of our top shared priorities, and I appreciate Mayor Scott’s partnership and the work being done across the city under his leadership. Yesterday’s meeting was an opportunity to discuss our efforts on behalf of the people of Baltimore – from strengthening public safety, to updating our infrastructure, to creating greater economic opportunity. This work is all the more important as the Trump Administration continues to attack our communities and essential programs that serve the City. I will continue to fight alongside Federal Team Maryland to deliver for Baltimore and to make progress on our shared goals to continue moving the City forward,” said Senator Van Hollen.

“I say it all the time: Baltimore has the best federal delegation in the country, and meetings like this one underscore their commitment to our city,” said Mayor Scott. “Each and every day, we're seeing the impact of investments they've secured, from our public safety progress, to our housing investments, to new schools, rec centers, and more all across Baltimore. Especially as we deal with an administration that's actively sabotaging cities across the country, we are so grateful to have this delegation fighting for us in Washington.”

“We’ve seen the news of continued progress in Baltimore, on everything from gun violence to how the Port of Baltimore continues to thrive, and it’s a story to be proud of. The city and its leadership have proven how success happens when you plan effectively and when you’re prepared to respond to the unexpected. Baltimore has shown the nation what you can accomplish when you stick together. Team Maryland on Capitol Hill is committed to fighting for Baltimore and working together. We will continue to find areas where we can coordinate effectively, and we’ll continue to do all we can to make sure Baltimore and all of Maryland has everything needed to thrive,” said Senator Alsobrooks.

“I was glad to join my colleagues in the Maryland Congressional Delegation to meet with Mayor Scott and discuss the achievements, challenges, and top priorities for the greater Baltimore area. I applaud Mayor Scott for his leadership that has had impacts far beyond the region. Our partnership is critical to ensuring Marylanders across the state can benefit from a growing and vibrant economy, and Team Maryland remains committed to working together to improve the safety and livelihood of all who call Maryland home,” said Congressman Hoyer.

“It was a productive opportunity for our Congressional delegation to meet with Mayor Scott again to discuss our priorities and the critical issues facing Baltimoreans today," said Congressman Mfume. "We discussed ongoing efforts to improve public safety, progress on the Key Bridge rebuild and B&P Tunnel, and the escalating negative impacts that the Big Ugly Bill is having on our Medicare, Medicaid, and SNAP benefits. I am incredibly proud to be a part of a team that is committed to working together to tackle difficult problems and deliver meaningful results for the people of our City and our State.”

“I’m grateful for Mayor Scott’s steady vision and partnership so we can keep delivering for Marylanders,” said Congressman Raskin. “From Baltimore to Bethesda, the tie that binds us is delivering services, lowering costs and protecting the rights of our people across the Free State as ICE and Border Patrol continue their reign of lawlessness and chaos in our communities."

“It was good to continue our focus on affordability and economic opportunities for folks in the greater Baltimore area and across the great state of Maryland with Mayor Scott and my colleagues in the Maryland Delegation. We look forward to assisting our state and local partners in ameliorating the economic climate through these very tough times,” said Congressman Ivey. “We must meet these challenges head on in unity of purpose. Today’s meeting reaffirms that continued aim.”

“The biggest priority for Baltimore families is the same as it is for families everywhere: lowering costs and making sure they have a fair shot at building a good life,” said Congressman Olszewski. “I appreciated the opportunity to connect with Mayor Scott and my colleagues on how we can better partner across all levels of government to deliver on that priority.”

###
title: Maryland Delegation and Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott Meet to Discuss Baltimore City Priorities

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Democratic Whip Katherine Clark (MA-5) appeared on CNN News Central to call out Republicans for refusing to rein in AI and highlight Democrats’ fight to lower costs for working people. Below are excerpts of the conversation.

On Republicans Refusing to Put Guardrails on AI:

“We should be here in DC — where I am today — but there are no Republicans around working on this very issue.

“We want to be the leaders in this technology, but we want it to benefit the American people. We want to protect jobs, and protect our kids, and develop a way to harness AI for good, and protect the American people from harm.

“What we have is a president who is out there berating Americans opposed to data centers in their communities, saying they are ‘backwards’ and will be ‘poor’ if they don’t get on board. Inviting in — not regulation and outside oversight over this powerful technology with all its benefits but its very real threats — instead, bringing in the heads of these companies and saying, ‘Okay guys, you just police yourselves. We’re sure that will work out fine.’ Meanwhile, the Trump family continues to enrich itself by investing in data centers and AI.

“So, we have a total lack of addressing this very real concern of the American people by the president and the Republican Party.”

On GOP Cancelling Votes Instead of Finding Solutions for Americans:

“Again, we want to be the leaders in this. But there are ways as we are working with experts and we should be here working on these solutions to answer what the companies say they want: outside regulation, outside audits of what they’re doing. That’s not just people they hire who work within their companies, but let’s have people outside evaluating what happened. We have set up agencies for this kind of review in transportation, in financial services, and this is something we need to come together as Americans to address.

“Meanwhile, Mike Johnson’s response was to send us home early, rather than tackling this very key issue that Americans are worried about. I hear about it everywhere I go in my district and everywhere I go in this country.”

On Pete Hegseth’s Incompetence:

“I am extremely concerned about where Secretary Hegseth is taking our military as we are at war in Iran — a war that the president and the secretary recklessly put us into without making the case to the American people. Without coming to Congress as required.

“Democrats three times have put forward War Powers Resolutions asking them to stop this war, to come and make sense of this for people.

“And what are we seeing? We are seeing them covering up casualties of our service members. What a disgrace for the secretary of defense to cover up those casualties. Then we are seeing the impacts of this war on Americans — whether it’s at the gas pump or the cost of diesel that is driving our farmers into debt. They are not sure if they’re going to be able to afford to plant because of this record high cost of diesel. And all of this is going to come home in continued rising prices of groceries and other goods that American families are already struggling to purchase.

“So, to have the secretary try and make this into some ‘it’s their appearance and their testosterone levels that count.’ It is their military readiness. It’s making sure we have enough munitions. It is having a clear mission that is defined and aligns with our national security needs. None of that is being met by this secretary and this president.”

On Democrats’ Fight for an Affordable America:

“We keep talking to the American people and listening to them. Our message is very clear: We see your family, and we’re going to fight for you. We’re going to fight to lower the cost of housing and groceries and gas. We’re going to fight to make sure that when you need healthcare, you can afford it and you can get it when and where you need it. And then we’re going to make sure that we are holding the crooks accountable, because [the] corruption we are seeing in this Republican Party has a real cost for the American taxpayers.

“It’s time to put the American people first. Put their priorities first. Put their voices back in these halls, here in the Capitol.

“We have great candidates who are connected to their communities, who understand how hard it is for people to get a foothold, never mind have success, in this economy.

“The terms I hear are ‘I’m drowning. I’m barely able to keep my head above water. I can’t keep treading water.’ This is not how we build security for American families… And when we win the majority, this is how we’re going to govern: with the American people front and center.”

Watch the full interview, HERE.

title: Whip Clark on CNN: Democrats Are Putting the American People Front and Center

U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24) and U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA) introduced the Ocean Protection and DDT Reduction Act, new legislation aimed at addressing the toxic industrial waste and pesticide pollution dumped off the Southern California coast.

For decades, industrial waste — including the pesticide DDT — was disposed of in ocean dump sites off California’s coast, particularly in the San Pedro Basin. The Ocean Protection and DDT Reduction Act establishes a structured federal study to assess the damage to the local marine ecosystem and develop comprehensive solutions to clean up the waste.

“The San Pedro Basin has long been the site of an underwater toxic waste dump. This toxic waste – which includes the pesticide DDT – has been very harmful to the health of local marine life and poses a risk to people who live and work near these waters,” said Rep. Carbajal. “As the representative of California’s Central Coast, I know firsthand how much our communities depend on a healthy ocean – from our fishermen and maritime workers to our tourism and coastal economies. We have a responsibility to protect these waters. I thank Senator Alex Padilla for joining me in introducing this bill as a first step in fixing this environmental tragedy.”

“Our communities deserve to know what's in the water off of the coast of San Pedro and what it means for our health, our fisheries, and our future. By putting NOAA's scientists and our leading research institutions to work mapping the contamination, tracking how it moves, and exploring cleanup through bioremediation, we can finally address this problem head-on,” said Sen. Padilla.

“For decades we used the ocean as a dumping ground for all manner of wastes including deeply-concerning industrial byproducts from DDT manufacturing. This proposed legislation takes an important step to address fundamental issues around the disposition, impacts and remediation options for those wastes. While California may be ground zero for this issue, the legislation provides a needed path to take lessons learned off California's coast and apply them to waste disposal sites that occur along all our Nation's coastlines,” said David Valentine, Norris Chair and Distinguished Professor of Earth and Marine Science, UCSB.

Specifically, the Ocean Protection and DDT Reduction Act would direct the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to monitor waste sites in the San Pedro Basin, study how toxic chemicals like DDT spread into the ocean food web, and build scientific tools to track ocean dumping.

NOAA, in coordination with the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and Department of Defense, may award grants to academic and research institutions to study:

Spatial mapping of contamination

Co-contaminants and chemical mixtures

Movement, fate, and breakdown processes

Bioaccumulation and biomagnification in ecosystems

The bill authorizes $6 million annually from Fiscal Year 2026 through Fiscal Year 2032 to carry out these critical activities.

Read the full bill text here.

title: Carbajal, Padilla Introduce Legislation to Investigate Toxic Waste Dump Off California Coast

NEWARK, NJ – Today, Congresswoman LaMonica McIver (NJ-10) announced the birth of her second child, a healthy baby girl. She released the following statement:

“Being a mom is one of the greatest joys of my life, and I feel deeply grateful to welcome this beautiful, healthy baby into the world,” said McIver. “There really aren’t words to describe how blessed my family feels to welcome a new life into the world. Getting the chance to raise a family is a priority and a delight for me, something I hope everyone who wants to, gets the chance to do. Bringing a child into the world is a reminder not only of why we fight for maternal healthcare and reproductive rights, but of why we fight for the rights and freedoms of our most vulnerable– they are someone’s babies too.”

McIver is only the fifteenth-ever member of Congress to give birth while serving. She also has a ten-year-old daughter and is one of only a small group of women serving in Congress with school-aged children.

She has shared her tumultuous reproductive health journey, including her battle with uterine fibroids, which required multiple surgeries. One such surgery had her in New Jersey in the morning and rushing to Washington, D.C., that same night to make it in time to vote on the House floor. These experiences have bolstered her deep commitment to advocating for women’s reproductive rights, and strong reproductive and maternal healthcare for all.

McIver is also in the middle of a legal battle, facing 17 years in federal prison from charges brought by the Trump Department of Justice (DOJ). The charges stem from a lawfully authorized oversight visit McIver conducted at Delaney Hall, the controversial immigration detention center in her district. The case is ongoing.

McIver is a strong supporter of the recent push for proxy voting for new parents, as she will not be granted any paid maternity leave from Congress. She will take the month of October to heal, be with her family, and bond with her new child. She plans to return to voting in November.

###
title: It’s a Girl! Rep. McIver Gives Birth To Her Second Child, A Symbol Of Hope For Her Family

FRESNO, Calif. – This week, Congressman Jim Costa (CA-21) led a bipartisan group of 14 members of Congress in urging the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to take immediate action to protect approximately $232 million in funding for the Section 502 Single Family Housing Direct Loan Program that is at risk of expiring at the end of Fiscal Year 2026.

In a letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins, the lawmakers called on the department to preserve funding Congress provided to help low- and very-low-income families purchase homes in rural communities. Recent reports indicate that USDA has obligated only a portion of the approximately $1 billion Congress provided for the program, leaving hundreds of millions of dollars at risk of going unused.

“These resources were provided by Congress to help families in rural America purchase homes and strengthen the communities in which they live and work,” wrote the lawmakers. “Regardless of party, we should share the goal of ensuring that congressionally appropriated funds are administered efficiently and reach the rural families they were intended to serve."

“The USDA's 502 direct mortgage program has been a flagship tool for increasing homeownership opportunities in rural places,” said David Lipsetz, President & CEO of the Housing Assistance Council. “To have these critical funds expire at a time when the program has been challenged with new and burdensome rules would be a real tragedy for rural families looking to buy a home. We applaud Congressman Costa and his colleagues for their leadership on this issue.”

The lawmakers also raised concerns about recent administrative changes that could limit access to the program and delay assistance to eligible families. They urged USDA to preserve the remaining funding, provide Congress with an accounting of unobligated balances, and take steps to improve loan processing and prevent future funding from expiring.

BACKGROUND
title: Costa Leads Bipartisan Effort to Protect $232 Million in Rural Homeownership Funding

Washington, DC — Representatives Ro Khanna (CA-17), Summer L. Lee (PA-12), and Chris Deluzio (PA-17) sent a letter urging the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center (UPMC) to bargain in good faith with nurses, nurse practitioners, and midwives at UPMC Magee-Womens Hospital after the lawmakers received reports raising concerns about staffing levels and patient care.
“We have received troubling reports from our constituents and organizers that nurses are routinely assigned more patients than nationally recognized clinical standards recommend. Nurses have described situations in which a single labor and delivery nurse may be responsible for two or three patients, even though established standards call for a patient in active labor to receive dedicated nursing care,” said the lawmakers.
The lawmakers also called on UPMC to make progress in contract negotiations with hundreds of health care professionals at Magee-Womens, who have been negotiating for months.
“For approximately eight months, nearly 900 health care professionals at UPMC Magee have been negotiating for a contract that reflects the critical role they play in caring for patients and families throughout western Pennsylvania. These workers have raised serious concerns about inadequate staffing, excessive workloads, and conditions that prevent them from consistently providing the level of care their patients deserve. UPMC has a responsibility to listen to these frontline professionals and work constructively to resolve their concerns without unnecessary delays,” the lawmakers continued.
title: Release: Representatives Khanna, Lee, and Deluzio Call on UPMC to Address Staffing Concerns and Bargain in Good Faith with Healthcare Workers

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) and Ayanna Pressley (Mass.-07) today introduced the Wigs for Warriors Act, legislation that would require TRICARE to cover cranial prostheses for individuals with alopecia areata and other non-cancer conditions that cause permanent or medically documented hair loss.

“I heard directly from a constituent, a 16-year-old from Prince William County and daughter of a U.S. Marine, who lost all of her hair to alopecia areata by the end of second grade. She told my team how a medical-grade wig could have helped her navigate the emotional and social challenges of losing her hair, but that these wigs can be incredibly expensive,” said Vindman. “This bill, which I am proud to lead alongside Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley, will help ensure TRICARE beneficiaries with alopecia areata, like my constituent, have access to the care and support they need to feel comfortable and confident.”

“When individuals in our military families experience severe hair loss, they should be met with the support and care they need to feel like their authentic selves,” said Pressley. “Through my own experience with alopecia areata, I understand the psychological, social, and economic impact that comes with navigating severe hair loss—and I know that we can do something to lighten the load. For some, accessing medical-grade wigs can make all the difference. That’s why I’m proud to lead the Wigs for Warriors Act alongside Rep. Vindman and bring much-deserved relief and support to TRICARE beneficiaries with alopecia areata and other hair loss conditions.”

TRICARE, the insurance for servicemembers and military families, has extremely limited coverage for individuals experiencing severe hair loss. Currently, patients with alopecia areata receive no coverage for a cranial prosthesis — a medical-grade, custom-fitted wig designed to address medically related hair loss.

The bill would require TRICARE to cover cranial prostheses for individuals with alopecia areata and other non-cancer conditions that cause permanent or medically documented hair loss, as certified by a physician. Coverage would also extend to hair loss resulting from chemotherapy, regardless of the underlying condition being treated.

The legislation would also eliminate TRICARE’s current lifetime limit of one prosthesis per patient, allowing cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy to receive coverage for multiple wigs as medically necessary.

“This act is life changing for both the military and medical hair loss communities, allowing for better mental health of our service members and their families,” said a 16-year-old resident of Prince William County with alopecia areata. “Representative Vindman and his team not only took the time to listen to my story but have moved forward to resolving the issue. I am forever grateful.”

The Wigs for Warriors Act is supported by the National Alopecia Areata Foundation (NAAF).

“The National Alopecia Areata Foundation applauds the introduction of the Wigs for Warriors Act of 2026 and thanks Representative Vindman for his efforts to improve the lives of members of the military and their families living with the autoimmune disease alopecia areata,” said Ryan Reczek, President & CEO of the National Alopecia Areata Foundation. “This legislation is critical to ensure that medically necessary cranial prostheses, also known as medical wigs, that are used to restore well-being and support mental health, are affordable and accessible under TRICARE.”

BACKGROUND

Alopecia areata is a common autoimmune disease that causes the immune system to attack a person’s hair follicles, resulting in patchy or complete hair loss across the scalp and body. Nearly 6.7 million people in the United States are directly affected by alopecia areata, with about 700,000 currently living with active disease. The remaining millions have had the disease or will likely develop it at some point.

Alopecia areata carries a substantial mental health burden and wigs are a documented, effective way to manage it. The psychological impact of alopecia areata can be profound, with elevated rates of anxiety and depression, increased time off work, and impaired quality of life, stemming largely from the fact that hair plays a crucial role in shaping an individual’s identity, self-esteem, and social interactions. This burden is especially acute for young people who develop the condition.

###
title: Vindman, Pressley Introduce Legislation to Expand Alopecia Support for Military Families

Raleigh, North Carolina – Rep. Deborah Ross (NC-02), Ranking Member Joe Morelle (NY-25), the top Democrat on the Committee on House Administration, and Rep. Valerie Foushee (NC-04) hosted a shadow hearing in Raleigh focused on the challenges facing North Carolina’s elections. A panel of experts, including Associate Justice Allison Riggs of the North Carolina Supreme Court, gave statements on the practical and legal challenges facing North Carolina’s election system.

This shadow hearing takes place amid widespread concerns over potential federal intervention of elections and voting restrictions proposed by Republican lawmakers and the Trump administration. This includes the push for the SAVE America Act and restrictions on voting by mail.

Experts at today’s shadow hearing included:

Associate Justice Allison Riggs - North Carolina Supreme Court

North Carolina Representative Robert Reives

Karen Brinson-Bell - Principal at Advance Elections

Terence Everitt - ED, NC Voter Protection Alliance.

Paul Cox – Partner at Poyner Spruill

John Hill - Senior Litigation Counsel at Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington

Virginia Kase Solomõn - President of Common Cause and the former CEO of League of Women Voters.

“While the state legislature tries to rig the rules, this administration is trying to sow chaos and undermine confidence in our elections. And with just over a month until election day, the president is still looking for new ways to disrupt Americans' ability to cast their ballots,” said Congresswoman Deborah Ross (NC-02). “North Carolinians should have confidence that their vote will count this November. But it is up to us to remain diligent. [...] In order for every vote to count—and to count equally—we need to ensure that North Carolinians are guaranteed fair and equal access to the ballot box.”

"In this moment, there is nothing more urgent than protecting American democracy,” said Ranking Member Morelle (NY-25). “The election is here and we are protecting Americans' right to the ballot box. Every time the Trump Administration has tried to interfere with the integrity of the midterm elections, they have lost.

Over the next month, we need to remain clear-eyed about the threats we continue to face. We will fight to protect American elections. Failure, quite simply, is not an option.”

“Election administration on every level has always been a fiercely debated topic, but in a world where modern technology creates both opportunities and challenges, the importance of properly addressing election security and protecting the right to vote is more important now than ever,” said Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04). “It is clear that the Republican party in Raleigh and in Washington want to use election administration as a way to make voting difficult and strenuous on voters.”

Washington, DC — Today, Congressmen Lou Correa (D-CA) and Jack Bergman (R-MI) reintroduced the VA Medicinal Cannabis Research Act. The bipartisan legislation directs the Department of Veterans Affairs to conduct clinical research on the safety and efficacy of medical cannabis in treating veterans’ post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and chronic pain.

"With the opioid crisis raging across America, it is imperative to the health and safety of our veterans that we find alternative treatments for chronic pain and service-related injuries," said Correa. "Throughout my district, I consistently meet veterans who depend on cannabis to manage their pain. Numerous veterans attest to the treatment benefits of medical cannabis. It's time the VA did a formal study and began recognizing that cannabis can play a safe role in our veterans' healthcare."

The bill would:

Authorize VA to implement a comprehensive research plan, including clinical trials assessing the effectiveness of medicinal cannabis in treating chronic pain and PTSD.

Expand research into related factors in veterans' health, including improvements to mood and social functioning, impacts on other substance use, and overall quality of life.

Require clinical trials to examine different forms, potencies, and methods of cannabis administration, with veterans' health and safety prioritized throughout.

“Veterans struggling with PTSD and chronic pain deserve access to treatments backed by sound science and rigorous research. The VA Medicinal Cannabis Research Act will help us better understand whether medicinal cannabis can provide safe and effective relief while ensuring Veterans’ health and safety remain the top priority. We owe it to our Veterans to explore every responsible avenue that could improve their quality of life,” said Bergman.

Chronic pain affects one in five Americans and impacts veterans at a higher rate than the general population. Twenty-three percent of veterans receiving VA care have experienced PTSD at some point in their lives, and the two conditions are often linked — veterans with chronic pain have elevated rates of PTSD. This bill would mandate research that could lead to safer, more effective treatment options for veterans managing these conditions.

"Since 2017, IAVA has made empowering veterans who are calling for the medicinal use of cannabis one of our top priorities. Our members have said consistently and passionately that cannabis offers real help with the most pressing injuries we face when we come home, from chronic pain to PTSD to traumatic brain injury. Our national policies are lagging, research is lacking, and the stigma persists. The VA Medicinal Cannabis Research Act is how we start to change that. Every solution begins with research, and veterans have waited long enough for it," said Kyleanne Hunter, CEO of Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA).

“The VFW supports the VA Medicinal Cannabis Research Act of 2023,” said Pat Murray, Director, National Legislative Service, Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW). “VFW members tell us that medicinal cannabis has helped them cope with chronic pain and other service-connected health conditions. They cannot receive these services at VA because of VA’s bureaucratic hurdles. VA uses evidence-based clinical guidelines to manage other pharmacological treatments of post-traumatic stress disorder, chronic pain, and substance use disorder because medical trials have found them effective. VA must expand research on the efficacy of non-traditional medical therapies, such as medicinal cannabis and other holistic approaches.”

View the bill text HERE.

text:
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, responsabilizó hoy al Gobierno por el aumento en la factura de luz que entra en vigor hoy. Una familia que consume 800 kilovatios-hora al mes pagará unos $42 más. El Comisionado Residente presentó cuatro alternativas para aliviar a las familias a corto plazo.

"Hoy las familias puertorriqueñas empiezan a pagar 18% más por la luz, y no es por mala suerte. Es el resultado de una reconstrucción lenta, de plantas averiadas y de un sistema que depende de una sola empresa para recibir el gas. La gente no puede seguir pagando los errores de otros", expresó el Comisionado Residente.

Nueve años después del huracán María, el 75% de los $14,300 millones en fondos federales obligados para la red eléctrica sigue sin desembolsarse, según la Oficina de Rendición de Cuentas del Gobierno federal (GAO). Mientras tanto, las plantas averiadas obligan a quemar diésel, un combustible mucho más caro.

"El Gobierno negoció con New Fortress un contrato de gas que la propia Junta de Supervisión Fiscal criticó por falta de competencia. Hoy esa empresa controla el única terminal por donde entra el gas a San Juan. Desde el 16 de septiembre las unidades 5 y 6 de la Central San Juan no reciben gas y estamos quemando diésel, que es cuatro veces más caro. El Negociado de Energía ya dejó fuera de la factura, por ahora, unos $75 millones vinculados a alegados incumplimientos de New Fortress, e investiga $19 millones en gas que Genera, su subsidiaria, habría pedido de más. El conflicto en el Medio Oriente ha empeorado los precios, pero no lo explica todo: el propio Negociado señaló plantas fuera de servicio y fallas en la entrega de gas", añadió el Comisionado Residente.

El Comisionado Residente propuso cuatro medidas inmediatas:

Que New Fortress responda por sus alegados incumplimientos. El Negociado de Energía dejó fuera de la factura, por ahora, unos $75 millones vinculados a los alegados incumplimientos de New Fortress. Esos costos no deben pasar nunca a la factura del pueblo.

Que el Gobierno asegure la entrada del gas y tenga un plan B. La demanda que presentó el Gobierno contra New Fortress es un paso, pero no basta. Hay que resolver ya la entrada del gas a San Juan y tener otro suplidor con contrato firmado por si New Fortress vuelve a fallar. Cada día que se quema diésel se paga en la factura de enero. El gobierno debe garantizar el suministro de gas finalizando su contrato de respaldo y comenzando a utilizar a los otros proveedores de GNL en la isla.

Que ADSEF aclare cuántos fondos federales de LIHEAP tiene disponibles. Este programa federal ayuda a pagar la luz a participantes de TANF y a otras familias de bajos ingresos que cualifiquen. ADSEF debe informar cuánto dinero tiene y cuándo abre las ayudas, ahora que más familias las necesitan.

Que el Gobierno identifique recursos para un alivio temporero. Si se encontraron $554 millones para el cheque de alivio contributivo, debe poder identificar recursos para aliviar la factura de luz mientras dure esta crisis, junto con incentivos para que las familias ahorren energía. Otras posibles medidas incluyen la reducción de la crudita y el trabajo a distancia. No obstante, urge que los alivios mantengan el presupuesto balanceado y que cada pérdida sea subsanada mediante recortes en otras áreas del presupuesto.

"Desde el Congreso he exigido que los fondos federales para la red se usen ya: he llevado el reclamo al Departamento de Energía federal con apoyo de republicanos y demócratas, y a Vivienda federal. También seguiré defendiendo en el Congreso los fondos de LIHEAP. Mi agenda es priorizar lo básico, y no hay nada más básico que prender la luz sin tener que escoger entre pagarla y comer", concluyó el Comisionado Residente.

###
title: Comisionado Residente responsabiliza al Gobierno por el alza en la luz y presenta alternativas

Washington, D.C. – Today, the Co-Chairs of the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition (SEEC) Building Resilient Housing Task Force Reps. Dave Min (CA-47) and Johnny Olszewski (MD-02) introduced the Community Disaster Protection Act, which would establish a five-year pilot program under the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to help local governments and community organizations design community-based catastrophe insurance that will help Americans in the most high-risk areas access affordable disaster coverage.

“As extreme weather becomes more frequent and severe, too many Americans are unable to obtain the insurance coverage they need to recover from a disaster,” said Congressman Johnny Olszewski. “The Community Disaster Protection Act takes a commonsense approach by helping high-risk communities close coverage gaps and make disaster protection more affordable. I’m proud to work with the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition (SEEC) and Congressman Min to help communities prepare for the challenges ahead, protect families from devastating financial losses, and build a more resilient future.”

“Families across the country are watching their insurance premiums skyrocket—or losing coverage altogether—because their communities are increasingly exposed to wildfires, floods, hurricanes, and other disasters,” said Congressman Dave Min. “We cannot wait until after disaster strikes to figure out how families and communities are going to recover. The Community Disaster Protection Act gives local communities new tools to close dangerous insurance gaps, invest in resilience, and develop coverage that actually reflects the risks they face. As these disasters become more costly, Congress has a responsibility to help ensure Americans are not left financially devastated simply because of where they live.”

“The Community Disaster Protection Act is a great first step to address the rising costs and unmet needs facing Americans, and EDF research makes clear that new and innovative solutions will be critical as climate change increases disaster risk. This bill will be essential to help more communities identify the solutions that meet their needs. By supporting locally designed pilots that pair insurance coverage with investments in risk reduction, The CDPA would support the development of insurance products that help high-risk communities secure affordable insurance coverage, incentivize effective disaster prevention, and provide greater stability to property insurance markets. We thank Representatives Min and Olszewski for their leadership and urge Congress to move this bill forward,” said Joanna Slaney, Vice President for Political and Government Affairs, Environmental Defense Fund.

“APCIA applauds Congressman Min and Congressman Olszewski for introducing the Community Disaster Protection Act, which would support community-based catastrophe insurance solutions, including parametric and other innovative risk-transfer models, to help close protection gaps and expand options for communities facing natural disasters,” said Sam Whitfield, Senior Vice President of Federal Government Relations and Political Engagement at the American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA). “Importantly, the bill recognizes that these approaches are intended to complement, not replace, the traditional, private property casualty insurance market. By encouraging risk mitigation, promoting community resilience, expanding access to financial protection, and testing new risk-transfer models, this pilot program can help communities prepare for disasters and speed recovery when disasters strike.”

“Architects are an essential part of the solution to helping communities prepare for growing disaster risks. The Community Disaster Protection Act will give communities new tools to better understand, manage, and insure against those risks—helping create the conditions for property owners and local governments to invest in the resilient buildings and infrastructure architects are uniquely equipped to design,” said Illya Azaroff, FAIA, 2026 National President, American Institute of Architects. “AIA is proud to support this legislation and looks forward to continuing our work with Representative Dave Min, Johnny Olszewski, and the SEEC Building Resilient Housing Task Force to advance practical solutions that strengthen communities before disasters strike.”

“As natural disasters continue to worsen in both intensity and impact across the country, we need innovative solutions to help communities and economies recover from devastation,” said Jessie Ritter, Associate Vice President for Water and Coasts at the National Wildlife Federation. “The Community Disaster Protection Act encourages proactive risk mitigation, while also giving communities a flexible solution to support recovery after disasters, particularly in areas that are the most vulnerable to extreme weather. We look forward to working with Representatives Min and Olszewski on this legislation.”

“CSAC looks forward to working with Congressmember Min on the Community Disaster Protection Act to advance practical, workable solutions for California communities. Local governments need more tools and flexibility to help protect families and residents facing growing disaster risks and insurance challenges,” said California State Association of Counties (CSAC) President and Santa Clara County Supervisor Susan Ellenberg.

Background

As climate change drives more frequent and severe extreme weather events, communities face widening disaster coverage gaps, making it harder and more expensive for them to rebuild. In 2024, economic losses from natural disasters in the U.S. reached $217.8 billion, approximately $105 billion of which was left uninsured. Rising climate-related damage has increased insurer payouts, driven up premiums, and prompted insurance carriers to withdraw from high-risk markets. Addressing this coverage crisis requires innovative approaches that expand insurance access, promote effective resilience, and strengthen the stability of insurance markets nationwide.

Communities are exploring ways to secure or facilitate insurance for a group of properties, leveraging their local knowledge and purchasing power to improve affordability, streamline enrollment, and incentivize risk mitigation tailored to local needs. These arrangements, known as community-based catastrophe insurance (CBCI), offer significant potential to close disaster coverage gaps but are only now beginning to be explored, with just a handful of U.S. jurisdictions currently piloting or implementing CBCI programs. For example, CBCI can be developed to act as a supplement to the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), such as a parametric flood insurance program, or to cover wildfire risk in communities where insurers are withdrawing coverage or declining to write new policies.

The Community Disaster Protection Act would promote the development of new disaster insurance products to help high-risk communities secure affordable coverage; incentivize effective disaster prevention; and provide greater stability to property insurance markets. It would direct FEMA to establish a 5-year pilot program to award competitive grants to local governments, quasi-government bodies, and community-based organizations to design, develop, implement, or facilitate CBCI.

Specifically, this bill would:

Close Disaster Coverage Gaps: Authorize grants to develop or facilitate CBCI products that cover disaster risks uninsured or underserved by traditional insurance; set actuarially justified premiums that enable broad participation; and prioritize applicants facing the greatest coverage gaps or disaster risks.

Preserve Local Flexibility: Allow funds to support a range of CBCI frameworks, without restricting the disaster risks or properties covered. Eligible uses of funds could include consumer outreach and education, catastrophe-risk modeling or research into disaster risks, and leveraging non-federal funds to support long-term program sustainability.

Promote Resiliency Investments: Require CBCI programs to promote specific individual or community-wide investments to mitigate disaster risks, reduce potential losses, and secure lower premiums.

Address Regulatory Ambiguity: Direct the U.S. Government Accountability Office to conduct periodic evaluations of program performance to determine the regulatory treatment of CBCI and other alternative insurance products with respect to federal disaster aid eligibility.

Preserve State Insurance Authority: Explicitly preserve States’ authority to regulate insurance markets and require all grant recipients to comply with applicable State insurance laws and regulations. Grants would only be a catalyst for CBCI arrangements operating within State regulatory frameworks.

This bill is endorsed by the American Property Casualty Insurance Association, American Institute of Architects, California State Association of Counties, Environmental Defense Fund, Evergreen Action, League of Conservation Voters, National Wildlife Federation, and Natural Resources Defense Council.

In addition, Reps. Ami Bera (CA-06), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Ed Case (HI-01), Kathy Castor (FL-14), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), Steve Cohen (TN-09), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Tim Kennedy (NY-26), Mike Levin (CA-49), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Deborah Ross (NC-02), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), and Shri Thanedar (MI-13) have joined as original cosponsors.

Text of the legislation can be found here.

A one-page summary can be found here.

###

The Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition (SEEC) is a coalition of 111 members of the U.S. House of Representatives that was founded in January 2009 to be a focused, active, and effective coalition for advancing policies that address climate change, promote clean energy innovation and domestic manufacturing, develop renewable energy resources, create family-sustaining clean jobs, protect our nation’s air, water, and natural environment, and promote environmental justice.

SEEC Co-Chairs are Reps. Doris Matsui (D-CA), Mike Quigley (D-IL), and Paul Tonko (D-NY).

text:
ICYMI: Rep. Salinas Joins KIND Press Call on Treatment of Unaccompanied Children
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) joined Kids in Need of Defense (KIND) for a virtual press conference on the Trump Administration’s efforts to fast-track the removal of unaccompanied children. Rep. Salinas raised concerns about children being held in prolonged detention, rushed through immigration court proceedings, and forced to navigate complex legal cases without adequate access to an attorney.
Salinas also highlighted her work in Congress to demand answers from federal agencies about prolonged detention, access to counsel, and policies that keep children separated from safe family members.
Listen to a recording of the full press conference HERE and read Rep. Salinas’ full remarks below.
Good morning. I’m Congresswoman Andrea Salinas, and I proudly represent Oregon’s Sixth Congressional District. Thank you to KIND for your work in standing up for children and for hosting today’s event.
Whether it is using prolonged detention as a tool to wear children down until they give up and self-deport, or rushing through court cases before a child can find a lawyer, the Administration is robbing these children of their due process and, in many cases, robbing them of their safety from serious harm.
These are children who have fled abuse, trafficking, or persecution in their home country. And instead of finding safety in the United States, a country that once proclaimed, “Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free,” they are being denied basic protections that could save their lives. Trump is using every tool he has, no matter how cruel, to meet his arbitrary deportation quotas, and children are paying the price. We owe them a fair chance to be heard and a safe place to stay while their cases are decided.
The Office of Refugee Resettlement, or ORR, is ground zero for Trump’s abuse. Congress gave ORR a clear mission: care for unaccompanied children and place them promptly with parents or other safe, vetted sponsors. Yet as of March 2026, children were spending an average of more than 200 days in ORR custody. That is more than six months when the standard under federal rules is twenty days.
My colleagues and I have raised concerns to the Administration about children remaining in custody even when a parent or another prospective sponsor has been vetted. We have demanded answers about ORR sharing information with ICE that can lead to the arrest of a parent or family member trying to reunite with a child. Just imagine the fear that creates for other relatives who might otherwise come forward.
Months of uncertainty in custody take their toll. Children can lose hope of seeing their families again. Prolonged detention can worsen anxiety and depression. It can also make it harder for a child to tell an attorney or a judge about the abuse or persecution they fled. And when a child sees no way out of detention, “voluntary departure” may no longer feel like a real choice.
At the same time, the immigration courts are intentionally speeding up children’s cases while access to legal help has been disrupted.
Just this week, CNN reported on a story from Texas where twenty-five children, some as young as three years old, appeared before an immigration judge. Fifteen of those children did not have an attorney, and even if they did, most 3-year-olds only have a vocabulary of no more than 500 words.
I’ve heard stories of children who are given only a week or two to find a lawyer, and of a child told to prepare and file an asylum application alone.
To make the situation worse, earlier this year, the Trump Administration allowed its contract with the Acacia Center for Justice (uh-KAY-shuh) to expire. I recently spoke with the Immigration Counseling Service, or ICS, who is a subgrantee of Acacia’s contract with ORR. Since 2008, ICS has served as Oregon’s sole legal services provider for unaccompanied children.
ICS told me that because the Trump Administration canceled longstanding contracts with immigration attorneys who represent unaccompanied children, organizations like theirs have lost a significant source of funding. The Administration is starving advocates and attorneys of resources. This loss of funding threatens the survival of both ICS and the unaccompanied children they represent.
Instead of continuing to work with longstanding legal partners, the Administration has signed a bridge contract with a new nonprofit who doesn’t have the capacity to represent all unaccompanied children, resulting in many children showing up to court without a lawyer. In other cases, lawyers haven’t spoken up as children faced the court.
A child cannot be expected to navigate a life-changing legal proceeding alone, especially while separated from family and living in prolonged detention. A fair hearing takes time. It takes language access with a vocabulary of more than 500 words, expertise from immigration lawyers who have the skills to work with unaccompanied children, and it takes a meaningful opportunity to get legal help and present evidence.
That is why I led 46 House colleagues in a letter demanding answers from ORR about prolonged detention, sponsor placements, children’s mental health, and its coordination with immigration enforcement. The Administration may not want to provide these answers. It does not want the American public to fully understand the grave harms to children its policies are causing, but I’m going to make sure the public knows what this Administration is doing to children.
I am also going to continue to press the Justice Department and immigration officials for answers about accelerated hearings, access to counsel, and the removal of children without a meaningful chance to present their cases.
ORR must return to its child welfare mission: vet sponsors thoroughly, make timely decisions, and release children to safe parents and loved ones without unnecessary delay. Immigration courts must give children a fair chance to obtain counsel and be heard. And we need federal agencies to answer for policies that keep families apart and put children at risk.
The United States should be a place where a child fleeing harm can seek safety and receive a fair hearing. I ask President Trump and this administration—where is your humanity? Show us the human side of your actions. That is the standard I will keep fighting for.
Thank you.
###
title: ICYMI: Rep. Salinas Joins KIND Press Call on Treatment of Unaccompanied Children

Washington, D.C. – Congresswomen Madeleine Dean (PA-04) and Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05) introduced a package of legislation to make American democracy more accessible for people with disabilities. Three bills will address accessibility issues in registering to vote, getting to the polls, running for public office, and serving in local government.

The Removing Access Barriers to Running for Elected Office for People with Disabilities Act would ensure people with disabilities do not lose their crucial, life-sustaining federal disability benefits when they campaign for elected office. Specifically, the bill would clarify to federal agencies administering disability benefits that campaigning for an elected office does not disqualify a person from receiving disability benefits.

The AID (Accessibility and Inclusion to Diversify) Local Government Leadership Act would provide local governments with an ongoing accommodations fund to ensure current and future elected officials with disabilities have access to needed accommodations to perform their duties. Eligible communities include those that are rural communities, have a population of less than 10,000 people or are communities with a population between 10,000 and 200,000 with a federal poverty rate of 18 percent or higher.

The Accessible Voting Act, also co-led by Congressman Jamie Raskin (MD-08), would support state and local efforts to improve voter accessibility and remove barriers to voting. Specifically, the bill would establish new programs for ensuring voting accessibility, including creating a national resource center on accessible voting and expanding the number of options for casting a ballot in federal elections.

“The ability to fully participate in our democracy is central to our American ideals—yet too often people with disabilities face unnecessary barriers to voting and public service,” Rep. Dean said. “This package of legislation will help ensure accessibility in registering to vote, getting to the polls, running for office, and serving in local government. WASHINGTON — Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31) and Puerto Rico Resident Commissioner Pablo José Hernández (D-PR) introduced the PROMISE for Small Businesses Act, legislation to enhance oversight of federal contracting and protect the commitments made to small businesses and their participation in subcontracting opportunities.

Currently, large companies and corporations that receive certain federal contracts are required to provide plans outlining how they will provide subcontracting opportunities to small businesses. This legislation directs the Small Business Administrator to conduct compliance reviews to ensure large contractors follow through on their promise to deliver opportunities to small businesses in their subcontracting plans.

“Small businesses are critical to our economy and they deserve a fair shot in the federal marketplace.” said Rep. Gil Cisneros. “I’m proud to join Rep. Pablo José Hernández to introduce the PROMISE for Small Businesses Act to make sure they are not being left out. If enacted, this legislation would strengthen oversight of federal contracts to help ensure that large prime contractors keep their promise to small businesses as outlined in subcontracting plans. It would direct reviews of subcontracting plans and require reporting to Congress on compliance, noncompliance trends, and any enforcement actions taken. We cannot allow our small businesses to be pushed out of federal contracting.”

“When companies receive federal contracts and commit to working with small businesses, we should make sure they follow through,” said Hernández. “These opportunities can help small businesses grow, create jobs, and build experience in the federal marketplace. Our bill strengthens accountability and helps ensure those opportunities reach them.”

Small businesses greatly benefit from competing in the federal marketplace, and this bill will ensure they’re able to continue to do so fairly.

The PROMISE for Small Businesses Act would require the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) to review at least 10 percent of contracts subject to these subcontracting plans at each federal agency every year to determine whether contractors are meeting their commitments.

The legislation would also require the SBA to report:

whether contractors complied with their small business subcontracting plans;

how many compliance reviews the agency conducted;

what compliance issues were identified; and

what additional actions or reviews the SBA took in response.

Full text of the bill can be found here.

Rep. Cisneros is a member of the House Committee on Small Business, the Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure, and on the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations. He is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and serves on its leadership team as the Freshman Representative.

###
title: Rep. Cisneros and Commissioner Hernández Introduce Bill to Strengthen Small Business Participation in Federal Contracts

Davids, Alford Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect America’s Medical Supply Chains, Support Kansas City Innovation
Bill would help protect medicine, vaccine, and animal health science from foreign influence
Today, U.S. Representatives Sharice Davids (D-KS-03) and Mark Alford (R-MO-04) introduced the Critical Biomanufacturing Input Assessment Act. It’s a bipartisan bill that would help strengthen America’s biotechnology supply chains, support the growing medical industry in the Kansas City region, and address growing concerns about U.S. reliance on foreign suppliers — including China — for critical materials needed to produce medicines and other health products.
“Kansas City is creating the next generation of medicines, health products, and technologies that improve people’s lives — and we need to make sure American companies have the supplies they need to succeed,” said Davids. “This bipartisan bill will help us identify weaknesses in our supply chains, reduce our dependence on countries like China, strengthen American manufacturing, and create good-paying jobs while lowering healthcare costs. I appreciate Representative Alford’s partnership on this important, bipartisan effort.”
“As we work to bring more manufacturing back to American soil, we must ensure our biotechnology supply chains are secure, transparent and resilient,” said Congressman Mark Alford (R-MO-04). “This commonsense, bipartisan legislation will help identify vulnerabilities, reduce reliance on foreign adversaries like China, and protect the critical materials needed to produce lifesaving medicines and animal health products. I’m proud to partner with Representative Davids to strengthen innovation in the Kansas City region and safeguard our nation’s health and economic security.”
Many products that Americans rely on — including medicines, vaccines, and animal health products — are made using biotechnology. But many companies do not have a clear picture of where the materials and equipment they depend on come from. Some critical supplies are made overseas, including in China, creating potential risks for our economy and national security. This bill will help identify these vulnerabilities before a disruption occurs.
The Critical Biomanufacturing Input Assessment Act would require the Department of Commerce to regularly review America’s reliance on foreign sources for important biotechnology supplies and equipment.
The information collected through this review would help:
- Identify potential supply chain problems before they become emergencies;
- Help businesses make better decisions about where to source materials;
- Encourage more companies to manufacture critical supplies in the United States; and
- Strengthen America’s ability to compete in the global biotechnology industry.
The Kansas City region is one of the country’s fastest-growing biotechnology hubs. It is home to the KC BioHub, a partnership focused on making Kansas City a national leader in biotechnology research, innovation, and manufacturing. The region is also home to the Kansas City Animal Health Corridor, one of the largest concentrations of animal health companies in the world.
These companies and research institutions rely on specialized supplies and equipment to develop products that improve human and animal health. Making sure those supply chains are strong and reliable is critical to their continued success.
Davids has been a strong supporter of expanding Kansas City’s biotechnology industry. She helped champion the region’s application for the federal Regional Technology and Innovation Hub program and has worked with KC BioHub and other local partners to support investments in biotechnology, workforce development, and advanced manufacturing.
title: Davids, Alford Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect America’s Medical Supply Chains, Support Kansas City Innovation

Rep. Gabe Vasquez Statement on Administration’s Illegal Decision to Withhold Funding
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On October 1, 2026, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) issued the following statement after the rescissions package announced by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB):
“The Administration is trampling on the Constitution by withholding funding approved by both parties in Congress,” said Vasquez. “Freezing this funding illegally withholds critical funding for New Mexico, including for rural housing, minority-owned small businesses, and for our students. This senseless order hurts New Mexicans and undercuts the will of the people and the ability of Congress to do its job. No matter how hard the President tries, he has no right to change the delegation of powers outlined in the American Constitution.”
This funding was approved with bipartisan support in Congress and is required to be allocated by the Administration by the end of the fiscal year. Instead, the Administration illegally issued a “pocket rescission,” withholding nearly $1 billion in approved funding. Some of the funding utilized in New Mexico includes:
- Funding for the College Assistance Migrant Program (CAMP), which provides students from migrant or seasonal farmworker families with academic support and counseling, allowing them to graduate high school and pursue higher education.
- Funding for the Housing and Urban Development Department to help New Mexicans learn how to buy, rent, or keep their homes.
- Funding for the Minority Business Development Agency, which helps minority businesses develop and grow throughout the state. One in four New Mexico businesses are minority-owned.
- Funding for the Department of Homeland Security and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services that supports local nonprofit and immigration processing, including health care and legal services.
